**Tafsir of Surah al-Waqi'ah**

It is a Meccan surah.

Abu Ishaq narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have grown gray!" He said, "Hud, al-Waqi'ah, al-Mursalat, 'Amma yatasa'alun, and 'Idhan-shams kuwwirat have made me gray." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3297).]]

Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in his biography of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with his chain to Amr ibn al-Rabi' ibn Tariq al-Misri, said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Abu Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, who said: Abdullah fell ill with the illness in which he died, and Uthman ibn Affan visited him and said, "What are you complaining of?" He said, "My sins." He said, "What do you desire?" He said, "The mercy of my Lord." He said, "Shall I not order a physician for you?" He said, "The physician is what made me ill." He said, "Shall I not order a gift for you?" He said, "I have no need of it." He said, "Will it be for your daughters after you?" He said, "Do you fear poverty for my daughters? I have ordered my daughters to recite the surah al-Waqi'ah every night, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him.'" [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. It was also narrated by Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (5/269) through Habashi ibn Amr ibn al-Rabi', from his father Amr ibn al-Rabi' al-Misri, with the same chain.]]

Then Ibn Asakir said: "This is what he said, but the correct reading is 'from Shuja'', as narrated by Abdullah ibn Wahb from al-Sarri." Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me that Shuja' narrated to him, from Abu Zabyah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." And Abu Zabyah would never leave it. [[Also narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/112) through Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Wahb with the same wording.]]

Similarly, Abu Ya'la narrated it from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Munib, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same wording. Then he narrated it from Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Munib al-Adani, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." He did not mention "Shuja'" in its chain. He said: "And I have ordered my daughters to recite it every night." [[Abu Bakr ibn al-Sunni also narrated it from Abu Ya'la in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla (no. 674).]]

Ibn Asakir also narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Nusayr and Uthman ibn al-Yaman, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Fatimah, who said: Abdullah fell ill, and Uthman ibn Affan came to visit him, and [the narrator] mentioned the hadith in full. Uthman ibn al-Yaman said: This Abu Fatimah was a client (mawla) of Ali ibn Abi Talib. [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal also narrated it from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, saying "from Abu Fatimah." It was recorded by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 2498). Al-Zayla'i, may Allah have mercy on him, criticized this hadith on four grounds, which together lead to its weakness: First, discontinuity (inqita'), as mentioned by al-Daraqutni and Ibn Abi Hatim in his 'Ilal, quoting his father. Second, the strangeness of its text, as stated by Imam Ahmad. Third, the weakness of its narrators, al-Sarri ibn Yahya and Shuja', as mentioned by Ibn al-Jawzi. Fourth, confusion (idtirab) in its transmission: some say "Abu Tayyibah" with an unpointed ta, some say "Abu Zabyah" with a pointed za, some say "Abu Fatimah," some say "Shuja'," and some say "Abu Shuja'." Imam Ahmad, Abu Hatim and his son, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn al-Jawzi, explicitly or implicitly, all agreed on its weakness. And Allah knows best.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, and Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the prayers in a manner similar to your prayers today, but he would make them lighter. His prayer was lighter than yours, and in Fajr he would recite "al-Waqi'ah" and similar surahs. [[Musnad (5/104).]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-Waqi'ah is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It was so named because of the certainty of its occurrence and its existence, as He says: ﴿Then on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾ [al-Haqqah: 15].

* *

His saying: ﴿There is no denying its occurrence﴾ means: there is no one who can turn it aside when Allah wills its occurrence, and no one who can repel it. As He says: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be turned back﴾ [al-Shura: 47]. He also says: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall, for the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–2]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the Day He says, "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ [al-An'am: 73].

The meaning of ﴿kadhibah﴾, as Muhammad ibn Ka'b said, is: "It must occur." Qatadah said: "There is no reversal in it, no turning back, and no return."

Ibn Jarir said: "Al-kadhibah is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-'aqibah and al-'afiyah."

* *

His saying: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ means: it will bring low some peoples to the lowest depths, to Hell, even though they were honored in the world, and it will raise others to the highest heights of 'Illiyyin, to lasting bliss, even though they were humble in the world. This is what al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Mus'ab al-Ma'ni narrated to us, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from his father, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it brings low some people and raises others.

Ubaydullah al-Ataki said, from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ — the Hour brought down the enemies of Allah to the Fire and raised the friends of Allah to Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It brings down men who were exalted in the world, and raises men who were abased in the world.

Al-Suddi said: It brought down the arrogant and raised the humble.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it makes the near and the far hear. Ikrimah said: It brings low and makes the nearest hear, and raises and makes the farthest hear. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said likewise.

* *

His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾ means: it will be set in motion with a motion, so it will quake and convulse throughout its length and breadth. Therefore Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said regarding His saying ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾: it will be violently convulsed [shadidan].

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It will be shaken with what is in it, like a sieve shaking what is in it.

This is like His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 1], and He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be pulverized into powder﴾ means: they will be crumbled into fine dust. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others.

Ibn Zayd said: The mountains will become like what Allah the Exalted described: ﴿heaps of sand, poured out﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14].

* *

His saying: ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding ﴿scattered dust particles﴾: it is the dust-cloud that rises and then vanishes, so nothing of it remains.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: al-habba' is what flies from fire; when it blazes, sparks fly from it, and when it falls it is nothing.

Ikrimah said: "Al-munbaththu" is that which the wind scatters and disperses. Qatadah said: ﴿scattered dust particles﴾ is like the dried-out tree that the winds scatter.

This verse, like its counterparts, indicates the removal of the mountains from their places on the Day of Resurrection, their departure, their movement, their uprooting (naskh, i.e., their pulling out), and their becoming like carded wool.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection people will be divided into three categories. A group on the right of the Throne: they are those who came out of the right side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will be taken to the right side. Al-Suddi said: They are the majority of the people of Paradise. Others on the left of the Throne: they are those who came out of the left side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their left hands, and they will be taken to the left side. They are the majority of the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us from their deeds. And a group of foremost ones (al-sabiqun) before Him. They are the most special, the most favored, and the nearest, of the companions of the right, who are their masters. Among them are the Messengers, the Prophets, the truthful ones (siddiqun), and the martyrs. They are fewer in number than the companions of the right. Therefore He said: ﴿So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾. Thus He divided them into these three types at the end of the surah, at the time of their death. And He mentioned them thus in His saying: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾ [Fatir: 32], the verse in full. That is according to one of the two opinions regarding "the one who wrongs himself," as has already been explained.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: He said: They are those mentioned in the surah of the Angels: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾.

Ibn Juraij narrated from Ibn Abbas: These three kinds are those mentioned at the end of this surah and in the surah of the Angels.

Yazid al-Raqqashi said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾, and he said: Three categories.

Mujahid said: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ [he said], meaning: three groups. Maymun ibn Mihran said: Three companies. Ubaydullah al-Ataki narrated from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: two in Paradise and one in the Fire.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir: 7]: "They are the similar ones; each man from a people who used to do their deeds." That is because Allah says: ﴿And you will be three kinds. So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾, and he said: They are the similar ones. [[The hadith will be cited at verse 7 of surah al-Takwir.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Bara' al-Ghanawi narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿And the companions of the right﴾, ﴿and the companions of the left﴾, then he gathered his hand into two fistfuls and said: "This is for Paradise, and I do not mind; and this is for the Fire, and I do not mind." [[Musnad (5/239). Al-Hasan did not hear from Mu'adh.]]

Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Do you know who are the foremost to the shade of the Day of Resurrection?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Those who, when the truth is given to them, accept it, and when it is asked of them, they give it, and they judge people by the same standard as they judge themselves." [[al-Musnad (6/67).]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abu Hamzah Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: they are the prophets, peace be upon them. As-Suddi said: they are the people of 'Illiyyin. Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: Yusha' ibn Nun, who preceded to Musa; the believer of the family of Ya-Sin, who preceded to 'Isa; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who preceded to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas, from Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Madaini al-Bazzaz, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Dahhak al-Madaini, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned, narrating to us, Mihran, from Kharijah, from Qurrah, from Ibn Sirin, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: those who prayed towards both qiblahs. [[In manuscript A: "Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned from..."]]

Ibn Jarir [[In manuscript A: "Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it."]] also narrated it from the report of Kharijah, with it.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾ means: from every nation.

Al-Awza'i narrated from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sawda that he recited this verse, ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near﴾, and then said: "The first of them to go to the mosque (in the morning), and the first of them to go out in the way of Allah."

All these statements are sound, for what is meant by "the foremost" is those who hasten to do good deeds as they were commanded. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and He said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 22]. Whoever races to this world, and precedes to good, will be among the foremost to honour in the Hereafter, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and "as you sow, so shall you reap." Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones brought near. In Gardens of Delight﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Our father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qazzaz al-Razi narrated to us, Kharijah ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The angels said: "O Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world, so they eat, drink and marry; so give us the Hereafter." He said: "I will not do that." They asked again three times, and He said: "I will not make those whom I created with My Hand like one to whom I said 'Be,' and it was." Then Abdullah recited: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In Gardens of Delight﴾. [[In manuscript A: "al-Fazari."]]

This report was also narrated by the Imam 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi in his book "ar-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyyah" [[In manuscript A: "'Umar."]], and its wording is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "I will not make the righteous offspring of those whom I created with My Hand like one to whom I said 'Be,' and it was." [[Al-Darimi narrated it as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, as in the author's al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (1/55), and said: "and it is more sound." It has a supporting report from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/48), who said: "This hadith is not sound."]]

They are the majority of the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us from their deeds. And a group of foremost ones (al-sabiqun) before Him. They are the most special, the most favored, and the nearest, of the companions of the right, who are their masters. Among them are the Messengers, the Prophets, the truthful ones (siddiqun), and the martyrs. They are fewer in number than the companions of the right. Therefore He said: ﴿So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾. Thus He divided them into these three types at the end of the surah, at the time of their death. And He mentioned them thus in His saying: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾ [Fatir: 32], the verse in full. That is according to one of the two opinions regarding "the one who wrongs himself," as has already been explained.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: He said: They are those mentioned in the surah of the Angels: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾.

Ibn Juraij narrated from Ibn Abbas: These three kinds are those mentioned at the end of this surah and in the surah of the Angels.

Yazid al-Raqqashi said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾, and he said: Three categories.

Mujahid said: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ [he said], meaning: three groups. Maymun ibn Mihran said: Three companies. Ubaydullah al-Ataki narrated from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: two in Paradise and one in the Fire.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir: 7]: "They are the similar ones; each man from a people who used to do their deeds." That is because Allah says: ﴿And you will be three kinds. So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾, and he said: They are the similar ones. [[The hadith will be cited at verse 7 of surah al-Takwir.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Bara' al-Ghanawi narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿And the companions of the right﴾, ﴿and the companions of the left﴾, then he gathered his hand into two fistfuls and said: "This is for Paradise, and I do not mind; and this is for the Fire, and I do not mind." [[Musnad (5/239). Al-Hasan did not hear from Mu'adh.]]

Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Do you know who are the foremost to the shade of the Day of Resurrection?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Those who, when the truth is given to them, accept it, and when it is asked of them, they give it, and they judge people by the same standard as they judge themselves." [[al-Musnad (6/67).]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abu Hamzah Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: they are the prophets, peace be upon them. As-Suddi said: they are the people of 'Illiyyin. Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: Yusha' ibn Nun, who preceded to Musa; the believer of the family of Ya-Sin, who preceded to 'Isa; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who preceded to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas, from Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Madaini al-Bazzaz, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Dahhak al-Madaini, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned, narrating to us, Mihran, from Kharijah, from Qurrah, from Ibn Sirin, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: those who prayed towards both qiblahs. [[In manuscript A: "Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned from..."]]

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾ means: from every nation.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and He said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 22]. Whoever races to this world, and precedes to good, will be among the foremost to honour in the Hereafter, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and "as you sow, so shall you reap." [[Al-Darimi narrated it as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, as in the author's al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (1/55), and said: "and it is more sound." **Tafsir of Surah al-Waqi'ah**

It is a Meccan surah.

Abu Ishaq narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have grown gray!" He said, "Hud, al-Waqi'ah, al-Mursalat, 'Amma yatasa'alun, and 'Idhan-shams kuwwirat have made me gray." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3297).]]

Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in his biography of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with his chain to Amr ibn al-Rabi' ibn Tariq al-Misri, said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Abu Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, who said: Abdullah fell ill with the illness in which he died, and Uthman ibn Affan visited him and said, "What are you complaining of?" He said, "My sins." He said, "What do you desire?" He said, "The mercy of my Lord." He said, "Shall I not order a physician for you?" He said, "The physician is what made me ill." He said, "Shall I not order a gift for you?" He said, "I have no need of it." He said, "Will it be for your daughters after you?" He said, "Do you fear poverty for my daughters? I have ordered my daughters to recite the surah al-Waqi'ah every night, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him.'" [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. It was also narrated by Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (5/269) through Habashi ibn Amr ibn al-Rabi', from his father Amr ibn al-Rabi' al-Misri, with the same chain.]]

Then Ibn Asakir said: "This is what he said, but the correct reading is 'from Shuja'', as narrated by Abdullah ibn Wahb from al-Sarri." Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me that Shuja' narrated to him, from Abu Zabyah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." And Abu Zabyah would never leave it. [[Also narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/112) through Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Wahb with the same wording.]]

Similarly, Abu Ya'la narrated it from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Munib, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same wording. Then he narrated it from Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Munib al-Adani, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." He did not mention "Shuja'" in its chain. He said: "And I have ordered my daughters to recite it every night." [[Abu Bakr ibn al-Sunni also narrated it from Abu Ya'la in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla (no. 674).]]

Ibn Asakir also narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Nusayr and Uthman ibn al-Yaman, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Fatimah, who said: Abdullah fell ill, and Uthman ibn Affan came to visit him, and [the narrator] mentioned the hadith in full. Uthman ibn al-Yaman said: This Abu Fatimah was a client (mawla) of Ali ibn Abi Talib. [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal also narrated it from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, saying "from Abu Fatimah." It was recorded by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 2498). Al-Zayla'i, may Allah have mercy on him, criticized this hadith on four grounds, which together lead to its weakness: First, discontinuity (inqita'), as mentioned by al-Daraqutni and Ibn Abi Hatim in his 'Ilal, quoting his father. Second, the strangeness of its text, as stated by Imam Ahmad. Third, the weakness of its narrators, al-Sarri ibn Yahya and Shuja', as mentioned by Ibn al-Jawzi. Fourth, confusion (idtirab) in its transmission: some say "Abu Tayyibah" with an unpointed ta, some say "Abu Zabyah" with a pointed za, some say "Abu Fatimah," some say "Shuja'," and some say "Abu Shuja'." Imam Ahmad, Abu Hatim and his son, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn al-Jawzi, explicitly or implicitly, all agreed on its weakness. And Allah knows best.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, and Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the prayers in a manner similar to your prayers today, but he would make them lighter. His prayer was lighter than yours, and in Fajr he would recite "al-Waqi'ah" and similar surahs. [[Musnad (5/104).]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-Waqi'ah is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It was so named because of the certainty of its occurrence and its existence, as He says: ﴿Then on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾ [al-Haqqah: 15].

* *

His saying: ﴿There is no denying its occurrence﴾ means: there is no one who can turn it aside when Allah wills its occurrence, and no one who can repel it. As He says: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be turned back﴾ [al-Shura: 47]. He also says: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall, for the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–2]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the Day He says, "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ [al-An'am: 73].

The meaning of ﴿kadhibah﴾, as Muhammad ibn Ka'b said, is: "It must occur." Qatadah said: "There is no reversal in it, no turning back, and no return."

Ibn Jarir said: "Al-kadhibah is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-'aqibah and al-'afiyah."

* *

His saying: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ means: it will bring low some peoples to the lowest depths, to Hell, even though they were honored in the world, and it will raise others to the highest heights of 'Illiyyin, to lasting bliss, even though they were humble in the world. This is what al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Mus'ab al-Ma'ni narrated to us, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from his father, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it brings low some people and raises others.

Ubaydullah al-Ataki said, from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ — the Hour brought down the enemies of Allah to the Fire and raised the friends of Allah to Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It brings down men who were exalted in the world, and raises men who were abased in the world.

Al-Suddi said: It brought down the arrogant and raised the humble.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it makes the near and the far hear. Ikrimah said: It brings low and makes the nearest hear, and raises and makes the farthest hear. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said likewise.

* *

His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾ means: it will be set in motion with a motion, so it will quake and convulse throughout its length and breadth. Therefore Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said regarding His saying ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾: it will be violently convulsed [shadidan].

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It will be shaken with what is in it, like a sieve shaking what is in it.

This is like His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 1], and He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be pulverized into powder﴾ means: they will be crumbled into fine dust. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others.

Ibn Zayd said: The mountains will become like what Allah the Exalted described: ﴿heaps of sand, poured out﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14].

* *

His saying: ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding ﴿scattered dust particles﴾: it is the dust-cloud that rises and then vanishes, so nothing of it remains.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: al-habba' is what flies from fire; when it blazes, sparks fly from it, and when it falls it is nothing.

Ikrimah said: "Al-munbaththu" is that which the wind scatters and disperses. Qatadah said: ﴿scattered dust particles﴾ is like the dried-out tree that the winds scatter.

This verse, like its counterparts, indicates the removal of the mountains from their places on the Day of Resurrection, their departure, their movement, their uprooting (naskh, i.e., their pulling out), and their becoming like carded wool.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection people will be divided into three categories. A group on the right of the Throne: they are those who came out of the right side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will be taken to the right side. Al-Suddi said: They are the majority of the people of Paradise. Others on the left of the Throne: they are those who came out of the left side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their left hands, and they will be taken to the left side. [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. [[Abu Bakr ibn al-Sunni also narrated it from Abu Ya'la in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla (no. 674).]]

Uthman ibn al-Yaman said: This Abu Fatimah was a client (mawla) of Ali ibn Abi Talib. [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. Imam Ahmad, Abu Hatim and his son, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn al-Jawzi, explicitly or implicitly, all agreed on its weakness. And Allah knows best.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, and Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the prayers in a manner similar to your prayers today, but he would make them lighter. His prayer was lighter than yours, and in Fajr he would recite "al-Waqi'ah" and similar surahs. [[Musnad (5/104).]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-Waqi'ah is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It was so named because of the certainty of its occurrence and its existence, as He says: ﴿Then on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾ [al-Haqqah: 15].

* *

His saying: ﴿There is no denying its occurrence﴾ means: there is no one who can turn it aside when Allah wills its occurrence, and no one who can repel it. As He says: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be turned back﴾ [al-Shura: 47]. He also says: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall, for the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–2]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the Day He says, "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ [al-An'am: 73].

The meaning of ﴿kadhibah﴾, as Muhammad ibn Ka'b said, is: "It must occur." Qatadah said: "There is no reversal in it, no turning back, and no return."

Ibn Jarir said: "Al-kadhibah is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-'aqibah and al-'afiyah."

* *

His saying: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ means: it will bring low some peoples to the lowest depths, to Hell, even though they were honored in the world, and it will raise others to the highest heights of 'Illiyyin, to lasting bliss, even though they were humble in the world. This is what al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Mus'ab al-Ma'ni narrated to us, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from his father, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it brings low some people and raises others.

Ubaydullah al-Ataki said, from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ — the Hour brought down the enemies of Allah to the Fire and raised the friends of Allah to Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It brings down men who were exalted in the world, and raises men who were abased in the world.

Al-Suddi said: It brought down the arrogant and raised the humble.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it makes the near and the far hear. Ikrimah said: It brings low and makes the nearest hear, and raises and makes the farthest hear. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said likewise.

* *

His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾ means: it will be set in motion with a motion, so it will quake and convulse throughout its length and breadth. Therefore Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said regarding His saying ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾: it will be violently convulsed [shadidan].

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It will be shaken with what is in it, like a sieve shaking what is in it.

This is like His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 1], and He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be pulverized into powder﴾ means: they will be crumbled into fine dust. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others.

Ibn Zayd said: The mountains will become like what Allah the Exalted described: ﴿heaps of sand, poured out﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14].

* *

His saying: ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding ﴿scattered dust particles﴾: it is the dust-cloud that rises and then vanishes, so nothing of it remains.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: al-habba' is what flies from fire; when it blazes, sparks fly from it, and when it falls it is nothing.

Ikrimah said: "Al-munbaththu" is that which the wind scatters and disperses. Qatadah said: ﴿scattered dust particles﴾ is like the dried-out tree that the winds scatter.

This verse, like its counterparts, indicates the removal of the mountains from their places on the Day of Resurrection, their departure, their movement, their uprooting (naskh, i.e., their pulling out), and their becoming like carded wool.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection people will be divided into three categories. A group on the right of the Throne: they are those who came out of the right side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will be taken to the right side. Al-Suddi said: They are the majority of the people of Paradise. Others on the left of the Throne: they are those who came out of the left side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their left hands, and they will be taken to the left side. They are the majority of the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us from their deeds. And a group of foremost ones (al-sabiqun) before Him. They are the most special, the most favored, and the nearest, of the companions of the right, who are their masters. Among them are the Messengers, the Prophets, the truthful ones (siddiqun), and the martyrs. They are fewer in number than the companions of the right. Therefore He said: ﴿So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾. Thus He divided them into these three types at the end of the surah, at the time of their death. And He mentioned them thus in His saying: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾ [Fatir: 32], the verse in full. That is according to one of the two opinions regarding "the one who wrongs himself," as has already been explained.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: He said: They are those mentioned in the surah of the Angels: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾.

Ibn Juraij narrated from Ibn Abbas: These three kinds are those mentioned at the end of this surah and in the surah of the Angels.

Yazid al-Raqqashi said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾, and he said: Three categories.

Mujahid said: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ [he said], meaning: three groups. Maymun ibn Mihran said: Three companies. Ubaydullah al-Ataki narrated from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: two in Paradise and one in the Fire.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir: 7]: "They are the similar ones; each man from a people who used to do their deeds." That is because Allah says: ﴿And you will be three kinds. So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾, and he said: They are the similar ones. [[The hadith will be cited at verse 7 of surah al-Takwir.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Bara' al-Ghanawi narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿And the companions of the right﴾, ﴿and the companions of the left﴾, then he gathered his hand into two fistfuls and said: "This is for Paradise, and I do not mind; and this is for the Fire, and I do not mind." [[Musnad (5/239). Al-Hasan did not hear from Mu'adh.]]

Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Do you know who are the foremost to the shade of the Day of Resurrection?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Those who, when the truth is given to them, accept it, and when it is asked of them, they give it, and they judge people by the same standard as they judge themselves." [[al-Musnad (6/67).]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abu Hamzah Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: they are the prophets, peace be upon them. As-Suddi said: they are the people of 'Illiyyin. Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: Yusha' ibn Nun, who preceded to Musa; the believer of the family of Ya-Sin, who preceded to 'Isa; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who preceded to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas, from Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Madaini al-Bazzaz, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Dahhak al-Madaini, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned, narrating to us, Mihran, from Kharijah, from Qurrah, from Ibn Sirin, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: those who prayed towards both qiblahs. [[In manuscript A: "Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned from..."]]

Ibn Jarir [[In manuscript A: "Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it."]] also narrated it from the report of Kharijah, with it.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾ means: from every nation.

Al-Awza'i narrated from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sawda that he recited this verse, ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near﴾, and then said: "The first of them to go to the mosque (in the morning), and the first of them to go out in the way of Allah."

All these statements are sound, for what is meant by "the foremost" is those who hasten to do good deeds as they were commanded. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and He said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 22]. Whoever races to this world, and precedes to good, will be among the foremost to honour in the Hereafter, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and "as you sow, so shall you reap." Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones brought near. In Gardens of Delight﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Our father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qazzaz al-Razi narrated to us, Kharijah ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The angels said: "O Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world, so they eat, drink and marry; so give us the Hereafter." He said: "I will not do that." They asked again three times, and He said: "I will not make those whom I created with My Hand like one to whom I said 'Be,' and it was." Then Abdullah recited: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In Gardens of Delight﴾. [[In manuscript A: "al-Fazari."]]

This report was also narrated by the Imam 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi in his book "ar-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyyah" [[In manuscript A: "'Umar."]], and its wording is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "I will not make the righteous offspring of those whom I created with My Hand like one to whom I said 'Be,' and it was." [[Al-Darimi narrated it as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, as in the author's al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (1/55), and said: "and it is more sound." It has a supporting report from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/48), who said: "This hadith is not sound."]]

It is a Meccan surah.

He said, "My sins." He said, "What do you desire?" He said, "The mercy of my Lord." He said, "Shall I not order a physician for you?" He said, "The physician is what made me ill." Mujahid said: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ [he said], meaning: three groups. Maymun ibn Mihran said: Three companies. Ubaydullah al-Ataki narrated from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: two in Paradise and one in the Fire.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Abi Thawr narrated to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir: 7]: "They are the similar ones; each man from a people who used to do their deeds." That is because Allah says: ﴿And you will be three kinds. So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾, and he said: They are the similar ones. [[The hadith will be cited at verse 7 of surah al-Takwir.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muthanna narrated to us, al-Bara' al-Ghanawi narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿And the companions of the right﴾, ﴿and the companions of the left﴾, then he gathered his hand into two fistfuls and said: "This is for Paradise, and I do not mind; and this is for the Fire, and I do not mind." [[Musnad (5/239). Al-Hasan did not hear from Mu'adh.]]

Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Do you know who are the foremost to the shade of the Day of Resurrection?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Those who, when the truth is given to them, accept it, and when it is asked of them, they give it, and they judge people by the same standard as they judge themselves." [[al-Musnad (6/67).]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abu Hamzah Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: they are the prophets, peace be upon them. As-Suddi said: they are the people of 'Illiyyin. Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: Yusha' ibn Nun, who preceded to Musa; the believer of the family of Ya-Sin, who preceded to 'Isa; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who preceded to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas, from Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Madaini al-Bazzaz, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Dahhak al-Madaini, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned, narrating to us, Mihran, from Kharijah, from Qurrah, from Ibn Sirin, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: those who prayed towards both qiblahs. [[In manuscript A: "Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned from..."]]

Ibn Jarir [[In manuscript A: "Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it."]] also narrated it from the report of Kharijah, with it.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾ means: from every nation.

Al-Awza'i narrated from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sawda that he recited this verse, ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near﴾, and then said: "The first of them to go to the mosque (in the morning), and the first of them to go out in the way of Allah."

All these statements are sound, for what is meant by "the foremost" is those who hasten to do good deeds as they were commanded. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and He said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 22]. Whoever races to this world, and precedes to good, will be among the foremost to honour in the Hereafter, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and "as you sow, so shall you reap." **Tafsir of Surah al-Waqi'ah**

It is a Meccan surah.

Abu Ishaq narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have grown gray!" He said, "Hud, al-Waqi'ah, al-Mursalat, 'Amma yatasa'alun, and 'Idhan-shams kuwwirat have made me gray." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3297).]]

Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in his biography of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with his chain to Amr ibn al-Rabi' ibn Tariq al-Misri, said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Abu Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, who said: Abdullah fell ill with the illness in which he died, and Uthman ibn Affan visited him and said, "What are you complaining of?" He said, "My sins." He said, "What do you desire?" He said, "The mercy of my Lord." He said, "Shall I not order a physician for you?" He said, "The physician is what made me ill." He said, "Shall I not order a gift for you?" He said, "I have no need of it." He said, "Will it be for your daughters after you?" He said, "Do you fear poverty for my daughters? I have ordered my daughters to recite the surah al-Waqi'ah every night, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him.'" [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. It was also narrated by Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (5/269) through Habashi ibn Amr ibn al-Rabi', from his father Amr ibn al-Rabi' al-Misri, with the same chain.]]

Then Ibn Asakir said: "This is what he said, but the correct reading is 'from Shuja'', as narrated by Abdullah ibn Wahb from al-Sarri." Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me that Shuja' narrated to him, from Abu Zabyah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." And Abu Zabyah would never leave it. [[Also narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/112) through Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Wahb with the same wording.]]

Similarly, Abu Ya'la narrated it from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Munib, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same wording. Then he narrated it from Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Munib al-Adani, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." He did not mention "Shuja'" in its chain. He said: "And I have ordered my daughters to recite it every night." [[Abu Bakr ibn al-Sunni also narrated it from Abu Ya'la in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla (no. 674).]]

Ibn Asakir also narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Nusayr and Uthman ibn al-Yaman, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Fatimah, who said: Abdullah fell ill, and Uthman ibn Affan came to visit him, and [the narrator] mentioned the hadith in full. Uthman ibn al-Yaman said: This Abu Fatimah was a client (mawla) of Ali ibn Abi Talib. [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal also narrated it from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, saying "from Abu Fatimah." It was recorded by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 2498). Al-Zayla'i, may Allah have mercy on him, criticized this hadith on four grounds, which together lead to its weakness: First, discontinuity (inqita'), as mentioned by al-Daraqutni and Ibn Abi Hatim in his 'Ilal, quoting his father. Second, the strangeness of its text, as stated by Imam Ahmad. Third, the weakness of its narrators, al-Sarri ibn Yahya and Shuja', as mentioned by Ibn al-Jawzi. Fourth, confusion (idtirab) in its transmission: some say "Abu Tayyibah" with an unpointed ta, some say "Abu Zabyah" with a pointed za, some say "Abu Fatimah," some say "Shuja'," and some say "Abu Shuja'." Imam Ahmad, Abu Hatim and his son, al-Daraqutni, al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn al-Jawzi, explicitly or implicitly, all agreed on its weakness. And Allah knows best.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, and Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Israil narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard Jabir ibn Samurah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the prayers in a manner similar to your prayers today, but he would make them lighter. His prayer was lighter than yours, and in Fajr he would recite "al-Waqi'ah" and similar surahs. [[Musnad (5/104).]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Al-Waqi'ah is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. It was so named because of the certainty of its occurrence and its existence, as He says: ﴿Then on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾ [al-Haqqah: 15].

* *

His saying: ﴿There is no denying its occurrence﴾ means: there is no one who can turn it aside when Allah wills its occurrence, and no one who can repel it. As He says: ﴿Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from Allah that cannot be turned back﴾ [al-Shura: 47]. He also says: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall, for the disbelievers, which none can avert﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 1–2]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the Day He says, "Be," and it is, His word is the truth. His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ [al-An'am: 73].

The meaning of ﴿kadhibah﴾, as Muhammad ibn Ka'b said, is: "It must occur." Qatadah said: "There is no reversal in it, no turning back, and no return."

Ibn Jarir said: "Al-kadhibah is a verbal noun (masdar), like al-'aqibah and al-'afiyah."

* *

His saying: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ means: it will bring low some peoples to the lowest depths, to Hell, even though they were honored in the world, and it will raise others to the highest heights of 'Illiyyin, to lasting bliss, even though they were humble in the world. This is what al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Mus'ab al-Ma'ni narrated to us, Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi narrated to us, from his father, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it brings low some people and raises others.

Ubaydullah al-Ataki said, from Uthman ibn Suraqah, the maternal cousin of Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾ — the Hour brought down the enemies of Allah to the Fire and raised the friends of Allah to Paradise.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It brings down men who were exalted in the world, and raises men who were abased in the world.

Al-Suddi said: It brought down the arrogant and raised the humble.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Bringing low, raising high﴾: it makes the near and the far hear. Ikrimah said: It brings low and makes the nearest hear, and raises and makes the farthest hear. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said likewise.

* *

His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾ means: it will be set in motion with a motion, so it will quake and convulse throughout its length and breadth. Therefore Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said regarding His saying ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾: it will be violently convulsed [shadidan].

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: It will be shaken with what is in it, like a sieve shaking what is in it.

This is like His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 1], and He says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj: 1].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be pulverized into powder﴾ means: they will be crumbled into fine dust. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others.

Ibn Zayd said: The mountains will become like what Allah the Exalted described: ﴿heaps of sand, poured out﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 14].

* *

His saying: ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: Abu Ishaq narrated from al-Harith, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding ﴿scattered dust particles﴾: it is the dust-cloud that rises and then vanishes, so nothing of it remains.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And it will become scattered dust particles﴾: al-habba' is what flies from fire; when it blazes, sparks fly from it, and when it falls it is nothing.

Ikrimah said: "Al-munbaththu" is that which the wind scatters and disperses. Qatadah said: ﴿scattered dust particles﴾ is like the dried-out tree that the winds scatter.

This verse, like its counterparts, indicates the removal of the mountains from their places on the Day of Resurrection, their departure, their movement, their uprooting (naskh, i.e., their pulling out), and their becoming like carded wool.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection people will be divided into three categories. A group on the right of the Throne: they are those who came out of the right side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will be taken to the right side. Al-Suddi said: They are the majority of the people of Paradise. Others on the left of the Throne: they are those who came out of the left side of Adam, and their books will be given to them in their left hands, and they will be taken to the left side. They are the majority of the people of the Fire, may Allah protect us from their deeds. And a group of foremost ones (al-sabiqun) before Him. They are the most special, the most favored, and the nearest, of the companions of the right, who are their masters. Among them are the Messengers, the Prophets, the truthful ones (siddiqun), and the martyrs. They are fewer in number than the companions of the right. Therefore He said: ﴿So the companions of the right — what are the companions of the right? And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? And the foremost, the foremost﴾. Thus He divided them into these three types at the end of the surah, at the time of their death. And He mentioned them thus in His saying: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾ [Fatir: 32], the verse in full. That is according to one of the two opinions regarding "the one who wrongs himself," as has already been explained.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾: He said: They are those mentioned in the surah of the Angels: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾.

Ibn Juraij narrated from Ibn Abbas: These three kinds are those mentioned at the end of this surah and in the surah of the Angels.

[[Musnad (5/239). Al-Hasan did not hear from Mu'adh.]]

Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Khalid ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Do you know who are the foremost to the shade of the Day of Resurrection?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Those who, when the truth is given to them, accept it, and when it is asked of them, they give it, and they judge people by the same standard as they judge themselves." [[al-Musnad (6/67).]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Abu Hamzah Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: they are the prophets, peace be upon them. As-Suddi said: they are the people of 'Illiyyin. Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: Yusha' ibn Nun, who preceded to Musa; the believer of the family of Ya-Sin, who preceded to 'Isa; and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who preceded to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Fallas, from Abdullah ibn Isma'il al-Madaini al-Bazzaz, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Dahhak al-Madaini, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih with it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned, narrating to us, Mihran, from Kharijah, from Qurrah, from Ibn Sirin, regarding ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾: those who prayed towards both qiblahs. [[In manuscript A: "Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad mentioned from..."]]

Ibn Jarir [[In manuscript A: "Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it."]] also narrated it from the report of Kharijah, with it.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost﴾ means: from every nation.

Al-Awza'i narrated from 'Uthman ibn Abi Sawda that he recited this verse, ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near﴾, and then said: "The first of them to go to the mosque (in the morning), and the first of them to go out in the way of Allah."

All these statements are sound, for what is meant by "the foremost" is those who hasten to do good deeds as they were commanded. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heavens and the earth﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133], and He said: ﴿Race to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden as wide as the heaven and the earth﴾ [al-Hadid: 22]. Whoever races to this world, and precedes to good, will be among the foremost to honour in the Hereafter, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, and "as you sow, so shall you reap." Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those are the ones brought near. In Gardens of Delight﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Our father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qazzaz al-Razi narrated to us, Kharijah ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The angels said: "O Lord, You have given the children of Adam the world, so they eat, drink and marry; so give us the Hereafter." He said: "I will not do that." They asked again three times, and He said: "I will not make those whom I created with My Hand like one to whom I said 'Be,' and it was." Then Abdullah recited: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In Gardens of Delight﴾. [[In manuscript A: "al-Fazari."]]

This report was also narrated by the Imam 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Darimi in his book "ar-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyyah" [[In manuscript A: "'Umar."]], and its wording is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "I will not make the righteous offspring of those whom I created with My Hand like one to whom I said 'Be,' and it was." [[Al-Darimi narrated it as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report, as in the author's al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah (1/55), and said: "and it is more sound." It has a supporting report from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/48), who said: "This hadith is not sound."]]

**Tafsir of Surah al-Waqi'ah**

It is a Meccan surah.

Abu Ishaq narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have grown gray!" He said, "Hud, al-Waqi'ah, al-Mursalat, 'Amma yatasa'alun, and 'Idhan-shams kuwwirat have made me gray." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3297).]]

Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir, in his biography of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with his chain to Amr ibn al-Rabi' ibn Tariq al-Misri, said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya al-Shaybani narrated to us, from Abu Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, who said: Abdullah fell ill with the illness in which he died, and Uthman ibn Affan visited him and said, "What are you complaining of?" He said, "My sins." He said, "What do you desire?" He said, "The mercy of my Lord." He said, "Shall I not order a physician for you?" He said, "The physician is what made me ill." He said, "Shall I not order a gift for you?" He said, "I have no need of it." He said, "Will it be for your daughters after you?" He said, "Do you fear poverty for my daughters? I have ordered my daughters to recite the surah al-Waqi'ah every night, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him.'" [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. It was also narrated by Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid (5/269) through Habashi ibn Amr ibn al-Rabi', from his father Amr ibn al-Rabi' al-Misri, with the same chain.]]

Then Ibn Asakir said: "This is what he said, but the correct reading is 'from Shuja'', as narrated by Abdullah ibn Wahb from al-Sarri." Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Al-Sarri ibn Yahya informed me that Shuja' narrated to him, from Abu Zabyah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." And Abu Zabyah would never leave it. [[Also narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi in al-'Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/112) through Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Wahb with the same wording.]]

Similarly, Abu Ya'la narrated it from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Munib, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same wording. Then he narrated it from Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il, from Muhammad ibn Munib al-Adani, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Abu Zabyah, from Ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites surah al-Waqi'ah every night, poverty will never afflict him." He did not mention "Shuja'" in its chain. He said: "And I have ordered my daughters to recite it every night." [[Abu Bakr ibn al-Sunni also narrated it from Abu Ya'la in 'Amal al-Yawm wa al-Layla (no. 674).]]

Ibn Asakir also narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Nusayr and Uthman ibn al-Yaman, from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, from Shuja', from Abu Fatimah, who said: Abdullah fell ill, and Uthman ibn Affan came to visit him, and [the narrator] mentioned the hadith in full. Uthman ibn al-Yaman said: This Abu Fatimah was a client (mawla) of Ali ibn Abi Talib. [[Tarikh Dimashq (vol. 294), Manuscript Institute edition. Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal also narrated it from al-Sarri ibn Yahya, saying "from Abu Fatimah." It was recorded by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman (no. 2498). He said: "Those who, when the truth is given to them, accept it, and when it is asked of them, they give it, and they judge people by the same standard as they judge themselves." [[al-Musnad (6/67).]]
