The scholars have differed over the meaning of His words ﴿the former﴾ and ﴿the latter﴾. It was said: by "the former" is meant the past nations, and by "the latter" is meant this Ummah. This is a report from Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri, which Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from both of them. It is also the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, who found support for it in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "We are the last, but the first on the Day of Resurrection."[[I did not find the hadith in Tafsir al-Tabari. The hadith is recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (896) and by Muslim in his Sahih under no. (885), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] He did not report anything other than this, nor attributed it to anyone.

Among what is cited in support of this view is what the Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim narrated: "My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Isa ibn al-Tabba' related to us, Sharik related to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the following was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise; rather, you will be half of the people of Paradise' – or: 'the half of the people of Paradise' – 'and you will share with them the second half.'"

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Aswad ibn Amir, from Sharik, from Muhammad, the seller of sheets, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, and mentioned it. [[Al-Musnad (2/391).]] Something similar has been related from the hadith of Jabir. The Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar: "Abd Rabbih ibn Salih related to us, from Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): When the following was revealed: ﴿So on that Day the Inevitable will occur﴾, in which was mentioned ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a company of the former peoples and a few of us?' He said: 'The end of the surah was withheld for a year, then there was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Umar, come and listen to what Allah has revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾. Indeed, from Adam to me there is a company, and my Ummah is a company, and we will never complete our company until we are aided by the black people, the camel herders, of those who testified that there is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner.'"

He narrated it thus, in the biography of "Urwah ibn Ruwaym", both its chain and its text.[[Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Asakir (11/q279), "photocopy of the Institute of Manuscripts".]] However, there is an objection concerning its chain. Many numerous routes have come with the Prophet's saying (ﷺ): "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," the hadith in its entirety. [[Among them is the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn, recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan under no. (3168), and the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/420).]] It is a standalone report in "The Description of Paradise", and to Allah belong praise and grace.

What Ibn Jarir chose here is open to objection; rather, it is a weak view, because this Ummah is the best of nations by the explicit text of the Qur'an, so it is far-fetched that those brought near would be more numerous in other nations than in it, unless the totality of the nations is compared with this Ummah. The apparent meaning is that those brought near from among this Ummah are more numerous than the rest of the nations, and Allah knows best. So the second view in this place is the preferred one: that what is meant by His words ﴿a company of the former peoples﴾ is: from the early part of this Ummah, and ﴿and a few of the latter peoples﴾ is: from this Ummah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Affan related to us, Abdullah ibn Bakr [[In A: "Bukayr", and in M: "Abu Bakr".]] al-Muzani related to us, I heard al-Hasan: He came to this verse: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near﴾, and said: 'As for the foremost, they have passed on; but O Allah, make us among the people of the right.'"

Then he said: "My father related to us, Abu al-Walid related to us, al-Surri ibn Yahya related to us, who said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In gardens of bliss. A company of the former peoples﴾, 'a company of those who passed away from this Ummah.'"

And my father related to us, Abdul Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari related to us, Abu Hilal related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, he said: "They used to say, or hope, that they would all be from this Ummah." So this is the view of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that the whole of them are from this Ummah. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than its last, so it is possible that the matter encompasses all nations, each according to its own measure; for this reason it is established in the Sahih collections and others, through more than one route, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best generation is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them," the hadith in its entirety.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (3651), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for the hadith narrated by the Imam Ahmad: "Abd al-Rahman related to us, Ziyad Abu Umar related to us, from al-Hasan, from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The likeness of my Ummah is the likeness of rain; it is not known whether its first part is better or its last part.'"[[Al-Musnad (4/319).]] This hadith, after ruling its chain to be sound, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion needs the first of the Ummah to convey it to those after them, so it needs those who uphold it at its later stages, and to establish people upon the Sunnah, transmit it and make it manifest; and precedence belongs to the earlier. Likewise a crop needs the first rain and the second rain, but the greatest reliance is on the first, and the crop's need for it is more emphatic, for without it the crop would not sprout in the earth, nor would its roots take hold in it. For this reason he, peace be upon him, said: "A group of my Ummah will continue to be victorious upon the truth, not harmed by those who forsake them nor by those who oppose them, until the Hour comes." And in another wording: "Until the command of Allah comes while they are still like that." The point is that this Ummah is more noble than the rest of the nations, and those brought near within it are more numerous than others and of higher rank, due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason it is established by mass transmission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he informed that in this Ummah there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning. In one wording: "With every thousand, seventy thousand," and in another: "With each one, seventy thousand."

The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: "Hisham ibn Marthad [[In H and the rest of the copies: "Yazid", and the correction is from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.]] al-Tabarani related to us, Muhammad – that is Ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash – related to us, my father related to me, Damdam – meaning Ibn Zur'ah – related to me, from Shurayh – that is Ibn Ubayd – from Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, there will certainly be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a host like the black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say: What came with Muhammad (ﷺ) is more than what came with the Prophets, peace be upon them.'"[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/297). In its chain is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak and did not hear from his father.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verse 13–26 (part 2 of 3):

It is fitting to mention here [at his saying: "A multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations" (56:13–14)] the hadith that the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah" (Proofs of Prophethood), where he said: Abu Nasr ibn Qatadah informed us, Abu 'Amr ibn Matar informed us, Ja'far [i.e., Ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mustafad al-Firyabi] narrated to us: Abu Wahb al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musarrih al-Harrani narrated to me, Sulayman ibn 'Ata' al-Qurashi al-Harrani narrated to us, from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'ah ibn Ribi'i, from Ibn Zaml al-Juhani, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he prayed the dawn prayer, would say, while folding his leg: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him. I seek the forgiveness of Allah; indeed Allah is ever Accepting of repentance," seventy times. Then he would say: "Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in a single day exceed seven hundred." He would say that twice, then turn his face towards the people. He liked dreams, and would say: "Has any of you seen anything?" Ibn Zaml said: I said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Good that you meet, and evil that you avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Relate your dream." I said: I saw all the people upon a wide, easy, level road, and the people were proceeding along the main path. While they were thus, that road rose up over a meadow I had never seen the like of, rippling, its water dripping, containing all kinds of herbage. He said: It was as if I saw the first caravan, when they reached the meadow, glorify Allah, then they made their mounts kneel on the road, and they did not deviate to the right or the left. He said: I seemed to see them proceeding. Then the second caravan came, and they were many times more numerous than them; when they reached the meadow they glorified Allah, then they made their mounts kneel on the road, and among them was the one who grazed and among them was the one who took a handful (of herbage). And they continued thus. He said: Then the great mass of the people came, and when they reached the meadow they glorified Allah and said: "This is the best of abodes." It was as if I saw them inclining right and left. When I saw that, I kept to the road until I reached the far end of the meadow, and there I was, with you, O Messenger of Allah, on a pulpit of seven steps, and you were on its highest step. On your right was a man, wheat-complexioned, straight-haired, aquiline-nosed; when he spoke he rose up, so that he surpassed the men in height. On your left was a man of medium stature, reddish-white, with many moles on his face, as if his hair had been bathed in water; when he spoke you all listened to him with honour. In front of them was an old man most resembling you in form and face; all of you were heading towards him and seeking him. In front of that was a lean she-camel, aged, and you, O Messenger of Allah, seemed to be driving her. He said: The colour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed for a while, then it passed from him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for what you saw of the smooth, wide, easy road, that is the guidance with which you were carried, and you were upon it. As for the meadow you saw, it is the world and the brightness of its life. I and my companions passed on without clinging to anything of it, and it did not cling to us, and we did not desire it and it did not desire us. Then the second caravan came after us, and they were many times more numerous than us, and among them was the one who grazed and the one who took a handful, and they were saved in that state. Then the great mass of the people came, and they inclined to the right and left in the meadow: Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we return. As for you, you passed on a righteous path, and you will not cease to be upon it until you meet me. As for the pulpit you saw with seven steps, and I upon its highest step, the world is seven thousand years, and I am in its last thousand. As for the man you saw on my right, wheat-complexioned and straight-haired, that is Musa (Moses), peace be upon him; when he speaks he rises above the men by virtue of Allah's speech to him. And the one you saw on my left, of medium stature, reddish-white, with many moles on his face, as if his hair had been bathed in water, that is 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary); we honour him for the honour Allah bestowed upon him. As for the old man you saw most resembling me in form and face, that is our father Ibrahim (Abraham); we all head towards him and follow him. As for the she-camel you saw, and you saw yourself driving her, she is the Hour, which will come upon us. There is no prophet after me, and no community after my community."
He said: After this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not ask anyone about a dream except that a man would come and relate it to him voluntarily.[[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (7/36). Its chain includes Sulayman ibn 'Ata' ibn Qays. Ibn Hibban said in al-Majruhin (1/329): "A shaykh who narrates from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'ah ibn Ribi'i, things that are fabricated, not resembling the narrations of the trustworthy; I do not know whether the confusion in them is from him or from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿upon thrones woven with gold﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., interwoven (marmulah) with gold, meaning woven with it. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others said likewise.
Al-Suddi said: interwoven with gold and pearls. 'Ikrimah said: latticed with pearls and rubies. Ibn Jarir said: from this is named the girth (wadin) of the she-camel that goes under her belly; it is fa'il in the sense of maf'ul, because it is plaited; and likewise the thrones in Paradise are plaited with gold and pearls.
And He said: ﴿reclining upon them, facing one another﴾, i.e., faces towards one another, none of them behind another. ﴿There will circulate among them youths made eternal﴾, i.e., they are made eternal in one state, they do not age from it, nor grow grey, nor change. ﴿With cups, and jugs, and a cup from a flowing spring﴾. As for al-akwab, they are the vessels without spouts or handles. The abariq are those that combine both descriptions. The ku'us are the goblets. All of it is from wine flowing from a running spring (ma'in), not from containers that run out and are emptied, but from flowing springs.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will not be affected with headache thereby, nor will they be intoxicated﴾, i.e., their heads will not ache and their intellects will not be taken away; rather it remains constant along with the exhilarating potency and the pleasure attained.
Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: in wine there are four qualities: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urination. Allah mentioned the wine of Paradise and freed it from these qualities.
Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Atiyyah, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿They will not be affected with headache thereby﴾ means: there is no headache of the head for them therein.
And regarding His saying ﴿nor will they be intoxicated﴾ they said: i.e., it does not take away their intellects.

* *

His saying: ﴿And fruit of what they choose, and the flesh of birds of what they desire﴾, i.e., they will be served with fruits of whatever they choose from among the produce.
This verse is evidence for the permissibility of eating fruit in the manner of choosing it, and the hadith of "Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb" supports this, which the hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in his Musnad: al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Narsi narrated to us, al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sawiyyah narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ikrash narrated to us, from his father Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb, who said: The Banu Murrah sent me with their zakat of property to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I came to Madinah and found him sitting among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. I came to him with camels like the roots of the arta-tree. He said: "Who is the man?" I said: Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb. He said: "Raise (your lineage) in genealogy," so I traced my lineage to "Murrah ibn 'Ubayd," and this is the zakat of "Murrah ibn 'Ubayd." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "These are the camels of my people, these are the zakat of my people." Then he ordered that they be branded with the brand of the zakat camels and added to them. Then he took my hand and we went to the house of Umm Salamah, and he said: "Is there any food?" We were brought a bowl abundant with thareed and wadhar, and he began to eat from it. I began to reach with my hand around its edges, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seized my right hand with his left hand and said: "O Ikrash, eat from one place, for it is one kind of food." Then we were brought a tray containing dates, or fresh dates—'Ubayd Allah was unsure whether it was fresh dates or dried dates—and I began to eat from in front of me, and the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) moved about the tray, and he said: "O Ikrash, eat from wherever you wish, for it is not one colour." Then water was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) washed his hand, and wiped with the moisture of his palms his face, his forearms and his head three times, then said: "O Ikrash, this is the ablution from what fire has changed."
Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it at length, and Ibn Majah narrated it in full, both from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Abu al-Hudhayl al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1848) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3274). 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ikrash has been criticised, and this hadith of his has been criticised. Al-Bukhari said: "His hadith is not established." Al-'Uqayli reported from him that he said: "There is a problem (nazar) in its chain."]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange); we do not know it except from his narration."

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz ibn Asad and 'Affan narrated to us—and al-hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Shaybān narrated to us—they said: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, who said: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) liked dreams, and whenever a man saw a dream he would ask about it if he did not know him; but if a well-known person praised him, he was more pleased with his dream. A woman came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw as if I was brought out of Madinah and was admitted to Paradise, and I heard a thud, to which Paradise trembled, and I looked, and there was so-and-so son of so-and-so, and so-and-so son of so-and-so," and she named twelve men whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent as a detachment before that. They were brought, wearing tattered garments, their veins flowing with blood. It was said: "Take them to the river al-Baydakh" or "al-Baydhakh." He said: They were dipped in it, and they came out with faces like the full moon. Then they were brought a golden dish containing dates, and they ate from its dates whatever they wished, and whichever way they turned it they ate whatever fruit they desired, and I ate with them. Then the messenger came from that detachment and said: "Our affair was such-and-such, and so-and-so and so-and-so were struck," until he counted twelve men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the woman and said: "Relate your dream," and she related it, and kept saying: "Then so-and-so and so-and-so were brought, just as he said."
This is the wording of Abu Ya'la. The hafiz al-Diya' said: this is upon the condition of Muslim.[[al-Musnad of Imam Ahmad (3/135); Musnad Abi Ya'la no. (3289), (6/44). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/175): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

The hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated to us, Rayhan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another grows in its place."[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/102). In its chain is 'Abbad, who has been criticised.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and the flesh of birds﴾. Imam Ahmad said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verse 13–26 (part 3 of 3):

Sayyar ibn Hatim narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the birds of Paradise are like the Bukht camels (a large breed of camel), grazing in the trees of Paradise." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed these are soft, pampered birds!" He said: "The one who eats them is more pampered than they are," saying it three times, "and I hope that you will be among those who eat from them." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [Al-Musnad (3/221).]

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Maqdisi related in his book "Sifat al-Jannah" from the hadith of Isma'il ibn 'Ali al-Khutabi, from Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Khuyuti, from 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn 'Asim, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ziyad, from Zur'ah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Ṭūbā (a tree in Paradise) was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Bakr, has it reached you what Ṭūbā is?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Ṭūbā is a tree in Paradise. No one knows its length except Allah. A rider would travel for seventy autumns under one of its branches. Its leaves are ḥulal (robes), and birds settle upon it like the Bukht camels." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there indeed a pampered bird there?" He said: "The one who eats it is more pampered than it, and you are among them, if Allah wills." [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/649).]

Qatadah said, regarding His saying ﴿and the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire﴾: It was mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see its birds are pampered just as its people are pampered." He said: "The one who eats them, by Allah, O Abu Bakr, is more pampered than them. Indeed they are like the Bukht camels, and I expect from Allah that you will eat from them, O Abu Bakr." [This is mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain), though it has also been transmitted through al-Hasan, likewise mursal, narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (12/13).]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to me, Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated to us, the son of my brother Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about al-Kawthar. He said: "It is a river that my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of jazur (slaughtered animals)." 'Umar said: "Indeed they are pampered!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who eats them is more pampered than they are."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from al-Qa'nabi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from his father, from Anas, and said: "Hasan" (good). [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2542, where he said: "hasan gharib" (good, strange).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a bird that has seventy thousand feathers. It alights upon the platter of a man of the people of Paradise, then shakes itself, and from every feather there comes out a color, meaning a hue, white like milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey, with no color resembling another. Then it flies away." [Hannad narrated it in al-Zuhd, no. 119, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us with it.]

This is a very strange hadith (ghari jiddan), and al-Wassafi and his shaykh are both weak.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to me: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Abu Hazim, from 'Ata', from Ka'b, who said: "Indeed the bird of Paradise is like the Bukht camels. It eats from what is created of the fruits of Paradise and drinks from the rivers of Paradise. They line up for it, and when it desires something of them, it comes until it alights before him. He eats from its outside and its inside, then it flies off, and nothing has been diminished from it." Sahih (authentic) up to Ka'b.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Indeed you look at the birds in Paradise and desire them, and then one falls before you roasted." [Juz' al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, no. 22. Humayd al-A'raj is munkar al-hadith (a narrator of rejected reports).]

* *

As for His saying ﴿and maidens with beautiful eyes, like hidden pearls﴾, some read it in the nominative (raf'), and its estimated meaning is: "and for them therein are maidens with beautiful eyes." The genitive (jarr) reading admits of two meanings. The first: that the i'rab (grammatical inflection) follows what precedes it through ittiba' (grammatical agreement by following), because of His saying: ﴿Immortal youths will circulate among them with goblets, jugs, and a cup from a flowing spring. They will not be affected by headache from it, nor will they be intoxicated. And fruit of whatever they select, and the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire, and maidens with beautiful eyes﴾, just as He said ﴿and wipe over your heads and your feet﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6], and as He said: ﴿Upon them will be garments of green silk and brocade﴾ [al-Insan: 21]. The second possibility: that it is among what the immortal youths circulate with, and the maidens with beautiful eyes are among them, but this takes place in the palaces, not among one another. Rather, in the tents, servants circulate among them with the maidens with beautiful eyes. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿like hidden pearls﴾, that is: they are like fresh pearls in their whiteness and clarity, as was mentioned in Surah al-Saffat: ﴿as if they were hidden eggs﴾ [al-Saffat: 49]. Their description has also been mentioned in Surah al-Rahman. Therefore He said: ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾, that is: this which We have bestowed upon them is a recompense for them for the good deeds they performed.

Then He said: ﴿They will not hear therein any vain speech or sinful talk, but only the word "Peace, peace"﴾, that is: they will not hear in Paradise any idle talk, meaning worthless speech empty of meaning, or speech containing a lowly or trivial meaning, as He said: ﴿You will not hear therein any idle talk﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 11], meaning no idle word. ﴿Nor sinful talk﴾, that is, no speech containing ugliness [in it]. ﴿But only the word "Peace, peace"﴾, that is: only the greeting of peace from some of them to others, as He said: ﴿Their greeting therein will be, "Peace"﴾ [Ibrahim: 23]. Their speech is also free from idle talk and sin.

He, the Exalted, says, informing about these foremost ones, that they are ﴿a company (thullah) of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾. The scholars have differed over the meaning of His words ﴿the former﴾ and ﴿the latter﴾. It was said: by "the former" is meant the past nations, and by "the latter" is meant this Ummah. This is a report from Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri, which Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from both of them. It is also the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, who found support for it in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "We are the last, but the first on the Day of Resurrection."[[I did not find the hadith in Tafsir al-Tabari. The hadith is recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (896) and by Muslim in his Sahih under no. (885), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] He did not report anything other than this, nor attributed it to anyone.

Among what is cited in support of this view is what the Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim narrated: "My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Isa ibn al-Tabba' related to us, Sharik related to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the following was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise; rather, you will be half of the people of Paradise' – or: 'the half of the people of Paradise' – 'and you will share with them the second half.'"

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Aswad ibn Amir, from Sharik, from Muhammad, the seller of sheets, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, and mentioned it. [[Al-Musnad (2/391).]] Something similar has been related from the hadith of Jabir. The Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar: "Abd Rabbih ibn Salih related to us, from Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): When the following was revealed: ﴿So on that Day the Inevitable will occur﴾, in which was mentioned ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a company of the former peoples and a few of us?' He said: 'The end of the surah was withheld for a year, then there was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Umar, come and listen to what Allah has revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾. Indeed, from Adam to me there is a company, and my Ummah is a company, and we will never complete our company until we are aided by the black people, the camel herders, of those who testified that there is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner.'"

He narrated it thus, in the biography of "Urwah ibn Ruwaym", both its chain and its text.[[Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Asakir (11/q279), "photocopy of the Institute of Manuscripts".]] However, there is an objection concerning its chain. Many numerous routes have come with the Prophet's saying (ﷺ): "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," the hadith in its entirety. [[Among them is the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn, recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan under no. (3168), and the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/420).]] It is a standalone report in "The Description of Paradise", and to Allah belong praise and grace.

What Ibn Jarir chose here is open to objection; rather, it is a weak view, because this Ummah is the best of nations by the explicit text of the Qur'an, so it is far-fetched that those brought near would be more numerous in other nations than in it, unless the totality of the nations is compared with this Ummah. The apparent meaning is that those brought near from among this Ummah are more numerous than the rest of the nations, and Allah knows best. So the second view in this place is the preferred one: that what is meant by His words ﴿a company of the former peoples﴾ is: from the early part of this Ummah, and ﴿and a few of the latter peoples﴾ is: from this Ummah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Affan related to us, Abdullah ibn Bakr [[In A: "Bukayr", and in M: "Abu Bakr".]] al-Muzani related to us, I heard al-Hasan: He came to this verse: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near﴾, and said: 'As for the foremost, they have passed on; but O Allah, make us among the people of the right.'"

Then he said: "My father related to us, Abu al-Walid related to us, al-Surri ibn Yahya related to us, who said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In gardens of bliss. A company of the former peoples﴾, 'a company of those who passed away from this Ummah.'"

And my father related to us, Abdul Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari related to us, Abu Hilal related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, he said: "They used to say, or hope, that they would all be from this Ummah." So this is the view of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that the whole of them are from this Ummah. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than its last, so it is possible that the matter encompasses all nations, each according to its own measure; for this reason it is established in the Sahih collections and others, through more than one route, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best generation is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them," the hadith in its entirety.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (3651), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for the hadith narrated by the Imam Ahmad: "Abd al-Rahman related to us, Ziyad Abu Umar related to us, from al-Hasan, from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The likeness of my Ummah is the likeness of rain; it is not known whether its first part is better or its last part.'"[[Al-Musnad (4/319).]] This hadith, after ruling its chain to be sound, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion needs the first of the Ummah to convey it to those after them, so it needs those who uphold it at its later stages, and to establish people upon the Sunnah, transmit it and make it manifest; and precedence belongs to the earlier. Likewise a crop needs the first rain and the second rain, but the greatest reliance is on the first, and the crop's need for it is more emphatic, for without it the crop would not sprout in the earth, nor would its roots take hold in it. For this reason he, peace be upon him, said: "A group of my Ummah will continue to be victorious upon the truth, not harmed by those who forsake them nor by those who oppose them, until the Hour comes." And in another wording: "Until the command of Allah comes while they are still like that." The point is that this Ummah is more noble than the rest of the nations, and those brought near within it are more numerous than others and of higher rank, due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason it is established by mass transmission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he informed that in this Ummah there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning. In one wording: "With every thousand, seventy thousand," and in another: "With each one, seventy thousand."

The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: "Hisham ibn Marthad [[In H and the rest of the copies: "Yazid", and the correction is from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.]] al-Tabarani related to us, Muhammad – that is Ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash – related to us, my father related to me, Damdam – meaning Ibn Zur'ah – related to me, from Shurayh – that is Ibn Ubayd – from Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, there will certainly be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a host like the black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say: What came with Muhammad (ﷺ) is more than what came with the Prophets, peace be upon them.'"[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/297). In its chain is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak and did not hear from his father.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verse 13–26 (part 2 of 3):

It is fitting to mention here [at his saying: "A multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations" (56:13–14)] the hadith that the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah" (Proofs of Prophethood), where he said: Abu Nasr ibn Qatadah informed us, Abu 'Amr ibn Matar informed us, Ja'far [i.e., Ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mustafad al-Firyabi] narrated to us: Abu Wahb al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musarrih al-Harrani narrated to me, Sulayman ibn 'Ata' al-Qurashi al-Harrani narrated to us, from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'ah ibn Ribi'i, from Ibn Zaml al-Juhani, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he prayed the dawn prayer, would say, while folding his leg: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him. I seek the forgiveness of Allah; indeed Allah is ever Accepting of repentance," seventy times. Then he would say: "Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in a single day exceed seven hundred." He would say that twice, then turn his face towards the people. He liked dreams, and would say: "Has any of you seen anything?" Ibn Zaml said: I said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Good that you meet, and evil that you avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Relate your dream." I said: I saw all the people upon a wide, easy, level road, and the people were proceeding along the main path. While they were thus, that road rose up over a meadow I had never seen the like of, rippling, its water dripping, containing all kinds of herbage. He said: It was as if I saw the first caravan, when they reached the meadow, glorify Allah, then they made their mounts kneel on the road, and they did not deviate to the right or the left. He said: I seemed to see them proceeding. Then the second caravan came, and they were many times more numerous than them; when they reached the meadow they glorified Allah, then they made their mounts kneel on the road, and among them was the one who grazed and among them was the one who took a handful (of herbage). And they continued thus. He said: Then the great mass of the people came, and when they reached the meadow they glorified Allah and said: "This is the best of abodes." It was as if I saw them inclining right and left. When I saw that, I kept to the road until I reached the far end of the meadow, and there I was, with you, O Messenger of Allah, on a pulpit of seven steps, and you were on its highest step. On your right was a man, wheat-complexioned, straight-haired, aquiline-nosed; when he spoke he rose up, so that he surpassed the men in height. On your left was a man of medium stature, reddish-white, with many moles on his face, as if his hair had been bathed in water; when he spoke you all listened to him with honour. In front of them was an old man most resembling you in form and face; all of you were heading towards him and seeking him. In front of that was a lean she-camel, aged, and you, O Messenger of Allah, seemed to be driving her. He said: The colour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed for a while, then it passed from him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for what you saw of the smooth, wide, easy road, that is the guidance with which you were carried, and you were upon it. As for the meadow you saw, it is the world and the brightness of its life. I and my companions passed on without clinging to anything of it, and it did not cling to us, and we did not desire it and it did not desire us. Then the second caravan came after us, and they were many times more numerous than us, and among them was the one who grazed and the one who took a handful, and they were saved in that state. Then the great mass of the people came, and they inclined to the right and left in the meadow: Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we return. As for you, you passed on a righteous path, and you will not cease to be upon it until you meet me. As for the pulpit you saw with seven steps, and I upon its highest step, the world is seven thousand years, and I am in its last thousand. As for the man you saw on my right, wheat-complexioned and straight-haired, that is Musa (Moses), peace be upon him; when he speaks he rises above the men by virtue of Allah's speech to him. And the one you saw on my left, of medium stature, reddish-white, with many moles on his face, as if his hair had been bathed in water, that is 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary); we honour him for the honour Allah bestowed upon him. As for the old man you saw most resembling me in form and face, that is our father Ibrahim (Abraham); we all head towards him and follow him. As for the she-camel you saw, and you saw yourself driving her, she is the Hour, which will come upon us. There is no prophet after me, and no community after my community."
He said: After this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not ask anyone about a dream except that a man would come and relate it to him voluntarily.[[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (7/36). Its chain includes Sulayman ibn 'Ata' ibn Qays. Ibn Hibban said in al-Majruhin (1/329): "A shaykh who narrates from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'ah ibn Ribi'i, things that are fabricated, not resembling the narrations of the trustworthy; I do not know whether the confusion in them is from him or from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿upon thrones woven with gold﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., interwoven (marmulah) with gold, meaning woven with it. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others said likewise.
Al-Suddi said: interwoven with gold and pearls. 'Ikrimah said: latticed with pearls and rubies. Ibn Jarir said: from this is named the girth (wadin) of the she-camel that goes under her belly; it is fa'il in the sense of maf'ul, because it is plaited; and likewise the thrones in Paradise are plaited with gold and pearls.
And He said: ﴿reclining upon them, facing one another﴾, i.e., faces towards one another, none of them behind another. ﴿There will circulate among them youths made eternal﴾, i.e., they are made eternal in one state, they do not age from it, nor grow grey, nor change. ﴿With cups, and jugs, and a cup from a flowing spring﴾. As for al-akwab, they are the vessels without spouts or handles. The abariq are those that combine both descriptions. The ku'us are the goblets. All of it is from wine flowing from a running spring (ma'in), not from containers that run out and are emptied, but from flowing springs.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will not be affected with headache thereby, nor will they be intoxicated﴾, i.e., their heads will not ache and their intellects will not be taken away; rather it remains constant along with the exhilarating potency and the pleasure attained.
Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: in wine there are four qualities: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urination. Allah mentioned the wine of Paradise and freed it from these qualities.
Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Atiyyah, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿They will not be affected with headache thereby﴾ means: there is no headache of the head for them therein.
And regarding His saying ﴿nor will they be intoxicated﴾ they said: i.e., it does not take away their intellects.

* *

His saying: ﴿And fruit of what they choose, and the flesh of birds of what they desire﴾, i.e., they will be served with fruits of whatever they choose from among the produce.
This verse is evidence for the permissibility of eating fruit in the manner of choosing it, and the hadith of "Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb" supports this, which the hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in his Musnad: al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Narsi narrated to us, al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sawiyyah narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ikrash narrated to us, from his father Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb, who said: The Banu Murrah sent me with their zakat of property to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I came to Madinah and found him sitting among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. I came to him with camels like the roots of the arta-tree. He said: "Who is the man?" I said: Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb. He said: "Raise (your lineage) in genealogy," so I traced my lineage to "Murrah ibn 'Ubayd," and this is the zakat of "Murrah ibn 'Ubayd." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "These are the camels of my people, these are the zakat of my people." Then he ordered that they be branded with the brand of the zakat camels and added to them. Then he took my hand and we went to the house of Umm Salamah, and he said: "Is there any food?" We were brought a bowl abundant with thareed and wadhar, and he began to eat from it. I began to reach with my hand around its edges, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seized my right hand with his left hand and said: "O Ikrash, eat from one place, for it is one kind of food." Then we were brought a tray containing dates, or fresh dates—'Ubayd Allah was unsure whether it was fresh dates or dried dates—and I began to eat from in front of me, and the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) moved about the tray, and he said: "O Ikrash, eat from wherever you wish, for it is not one colour." Then water was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) washed his hand, and wiped with the moisture of his palms his face, his forearms and his head three times, then said: "O Ikrash, this is the ablution from what fire has changed."
Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it at length, and Ibn Majah narrated it in full, both from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Abu al-Hudhayl al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1848) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3274). 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ikrash has been criticised, and this hadith of his has been criticised. Al-Bukhari said: "His hadith is not established." Al-'Uqayli reported from him that he said: "There is a problem (nazar) in its chain."]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange); we do not know it except from his narration."

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz ibn Asad and 'Affan narrated to us—and al-hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Shaybān narrated to us—they said: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, who said: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) liked dreams, and whenever a man saw a dream he would ask about it if he did not know him; but if a well-known person praised him, he was more pleased with his dream. A woman came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw as if I was brought out of Madinah and was admitted to Paradise, and I heard a thud, to which Paradise trembled, and I looked, and there was so-and-so son of so-and-so, and so-and-so son of so-and-so," and she named twelve men whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent as a detachment before that. They were brought, wearing tattered garments, their veins flowing with blood. It was said: "Take them to the river al-Baydakh" or "al-Baydhakh." He said: They were dipped in it, and they came out with faces like the full moon. Then they were brought a golden dish containing dates, and they ate from its dates whatever they wished, and whichever way they turned it they ate whatever fruit they desired, and I ate with them. Then the messenger came from that detachment and said: "Our affair was such-and-such, and so-and-so and so-and-so were struck," until he counted twelve men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the woman and said: "Relate your dream," and she related it, and kept saying: "Then so-and-so and so-and-so were brought, just as he said."
This is the wording of Abu Ya'la. The hafiz al-Diya' said: this is upon the condition of Muslim.[[al-Musnad of Imam Ahmad (3/135); Musnad Abi Ya'la no. (3289), (6/44). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/175): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

The hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated to us, Rayhan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another grows in its place."[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/102). In its chain is 'Abbad, who has been criticised.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and the flesh of birds﴾. Imam Ahmad said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verse 13–26 (part 3 of 3):

Sayyar ibn Hatim narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the birds of Paradise are like the Bukht camels (a large breed of camel), grazing in the trees of Paradise." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed these are soft, pampered birds!" He said: "The one who eats them is more pampered than they are," saying it three times, "and I hope that you will be among those who eat from them." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [Al-Musnad (3/221).]

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Maqdisi related in his book "Sifat al-Jannah" from the hadith of Isma'il ibn 'Ali al-Khutabi, from Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Khuyuti, from 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn 'Asim, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ziyad, from Zur'ah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Ṭūbā (a tree in Paradise) was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Bakr, has it reached you what Ṭūbā is?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Ṭūbā is a tree in Paradise. No one knows its length except Allah. A rider would travel for seventy autumns under one of its branches. Its leaves are ḥulal (robes), and birds settle upon it like the Bukht camels." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there indeed a pampered bird there?" He said: "The one who eats it is more pampered than it, and you are among them, if Allah wills." [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/649).]

Qatadah said, regarding His saying ﴿and the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire﴾: It was mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see its birds are pampered just as its people are pampered." He said: "The one who eats them, by Allah, O Abu Bakr, is more pampered than them. Indeed they are like the Bukht camels, and I expect from Allah that you will eat from them, O Abu Bakr." [This is mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain), though it has also been transmitted through al-Hasan, likewise mursal, narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (12/13).]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to me, Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated to us, the son of my brother Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about al-Kawthar. He said: "It is a river that my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of jazur (slaughtered animals)." 'Umar said: "Indeed they are pampered!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who eats them is more pampered than they are."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from al-Qa'nabi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from his father, from Anas, and said: "Hasan" (good). [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2542, where he said: "hasan gharib" (good, strange).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in Paradise there is a bird that has seventy thousand feathers. It alights upon the platter of a man of the people of Paradise, then shakes itself, and from every feather there comes out a color, meaning a hue, white like milk, softer than butter, and sweeter than honey, with no color resembling another. Then it flies away." [Hannad narrated it in al-Zuhd, no. 119, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us with it.]

This is a very strange hadith (ghari jiddan), and al-Wassafi and his shaykh are both weak.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to me: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Abu Hazim, from 'Ata', from Ka'b, who said: "Indeed the bird of Paradise is like the Bukht camels. It eats from what is created of the fruits of Paradise and drinks from the rivers of Paradise. They line up for it, and when it desires something of them, it comes until it alights before him. He eats from its outside and its inside, then it flies off, and nothing has been diminished from it." Sahih (authentic) up to Ka'b.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Indeed you look at the birds in Paradise and desire them, and then one falls before you roasted." [Juz' al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, no. 22. Humayd al-A'raj is munkar al-hadith (a narrator of rejected reports).]

* *

As for His saying ﴿and maidens with beautiful eyes, like hidden pearls﴾, some read it in the nominative (raf'), and its estimated meaning is: "and for them therein are maidens with beautiful eyes." The genitive (jarr) reading admits of two meanings. The first: that the i'rab (grammatical inflection) follows what precedes it through ittiba' (grammatical agreement by following), because of His saying: ﴿Immortal youths will circulate among them with goblets, jugs, and a cup from a flowing spring. They will not be affected by headache from it, nor will they be intoxicated. And fruit of whatever they select, and the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire, and maidens with beautiful eyes﴾, just as He said ﴿and wipe over your heads and your feet﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6], and as He said: ﴿Upon them will be garments of green silk and brocade﴾ [al-Insan: 21]. The second possibility: that it is among what the immortal youths circulate with, and the maidens with beautiful eyes are among them, but this takes place in the palaces, not among one another. Rather, in the tents, servants circulate among them with the maidens with beautiful eyes. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿like hidden pearls﴾, that is: they are like fresh pearls in their whiteness and clarity, as was mentioned in Surah al-Saffat: ﴿as if they were hidden eggs﴾ [al-Saffat: 49]. Their description has also been mentioned in Surah al-Rahman. Therefore He said: ﴿as a reward for what they used to do﴾, that is: this which We have bestowed upon them is a recompense for them for the good deeds they performed.

Then He said: ﴿They will not hear therein any vain speech or sinful talk, but only the word "Peace, peace"﴾, that is: they will not hear in Paradise any idle talk, meaning worthless speech empty of meaning, or speech containing a lowly or trivial meaning, as He said: ﴿You will not hear therein any idle talk﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 11], meaning no idle word. ﴿Nor sinful talk﴾, that is, no speech containing ugliness [in it]. ﴿But only the word "Peace, peace"﴾, that is: only the greeting of peace from some of them to others, as He said: ﴿Their greeting therein will be, "Peace"﴾ [Ibrahim: 23]. Their speech is also free from idle talk and sin.

He, the Exalted, says, informing about these foremost ones, that they are ﴿a company (thullah) of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾. The scholars have differed over the meaning of His words ﴿the former﴾ and ﴿the latter﴾. It was said: by "the former" is meant the past nations, and by "the latter" is meant this Ummah. This is a report from Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri, which Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from both of them. It is also the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, who found support for it in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "We are the last, but the first on the Day of Resurrection."[[I did not find the hadith in Tafsir al-Tabari. The hadith is recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (896) and by Muslim in his Sahih under no. (885), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]] He did not report anything other than this, nor attributed it to anyone.

Among what is cited in support of this view is what the Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim narrated: "My father related to us, Muhammad ibn Isa ibn al-Tabba' related to us, Sharik related to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the following was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise, a third of the people of Paradise; rather, you will be half of the people of Paradise' – or: 'the half of the people of Paradise' – 'and you will share with them the second half.'"

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Aswad ibn Amir, from Sharik, from Muhammad, the seller of sheets, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, and mentioned it. [[Al-Musnad (2/391).]] Something similar has been related from the hadith of Jabir. The Hafiz Ibn Asakir narrated it through the route of Hisham ibn Ammar: "Abd Rabbih ibn Salih related to us, from Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): When the following was revealed: ﴿So on that Day the Inevitable will occur﴾, in which was mentioned ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, Umar said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a company of the former peoples and a few of us?' He said: 'The end of the surah was withheld for a year, then there was revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Umar, come and listen to what Allah has revealed: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a company of the latter peoples﴾. Indeed, from Adam to me there is a company, and my Ummah is a company, and we will never complete our company until we are aided by the black people, the camel herders, of those who testified that there is no god but Allah, alone, with no partner.'"

He narrated it thus, in the biography of "Urwah ibn Ruwaym", both its chain and its text.[[Tarikh Dimashq by Ibn Asakir (11/q279), "photocopy of the Institute of Manuscripts".]] However, there is an objection concerning its chain. Many numerous routes have come with the Prophet's saying (ﷺ): "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise," the hadith in its entirety. [[Among them is the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn, recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan under no. (3168), and the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/420).]] It is a standalone report in "The Description of Paradise", and to Allah belong praise and grace.

What Ibn Jarir chose here is open to objection; rather, it is a weak view, because this Ummah is the best of nations by the explicit text of the Qur'an, so it is far-fetched that those brought near would be more numerous in other nations than in it, unless the totality of the nations is compared with this Ummah. The apparent meaning is that those brought near from among this Ummah are more numerous than the rest of the nations, and Allah knows best. So the second view in this place is the preferred one: that what is meant by His words ﴿a company of the former peoples﴾ is: from the early part of this Ummah, and ﴿and a few of the latter peoples﴾ is: from this Ummah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, Affan related to us, Abdullah ibn Bakr [[In A: "Bukayr", and in M: "Abu Bakr".]] al-Muzani related to us, I heard al-Hasan: He came to this verse: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near﴾, and said: 'As for the foremost, they have passed on; but O Allah, make us among the people of the right.'"

Then he said: "My father related to us, Abu al-Walid related to us, al-Surri ibn Yahya related to us, who said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost. Those are the ones brought near. In gardens of bliss. A company of the former peoples﴾, 'a company of those who passed away from this Ummah.'"

And my father related to us, Abdul Aziz ibn al-Mughirah al-Manqari related to us, Abu Hilal related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿a company of the former peoples, and a few of the latter peoples﴾, he said: "They used to say, or hope, that they would all be from this Ummah." So this is the view of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, that the whole of them are from this Ummah. There is no doubt that the first of every nation is better than its last, so it is possible that the matter encompasses all nations, each according to its own measure; for this reason it is established in the Sahih collections and others, through more than one route, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best generation is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them," the hadith in its entirety.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih under no. (3651), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

As for the hadith narrated by the Imam Ahmad: "Abd al-Rahman related to us, Ziyad Abu Umar related to us, from al-Hasan, from Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The likeness of my Ummah is the likeness of rain; it is not known whether its first part is better or its last part.'"[[Al-Musnad (4/319).]] This hadith, after ruling its chain to be sound, is to be understood as meaning that just as the religion needs the first of the Ummah to convey it to those after them, so it needs those who uphold it at its later stages, and to establish people upon the Sunnah, transmit it and make it manifest; and precedence belongs to the earlier. Likewise a crop needs the first rain and the second rain, but the greatest reliance is on the first, and the crop's need for it is more emphatic, for without it the crop would not sprout in the earth, nor would its roots take hold in it. For this reason he, peace be upon him, said: "A group of my Ummah will continue to be victorious upon the truth, not harmed by those who forsake them nor by those who oppose them, until the Hour comes." And in another wording: "Until the command of Allah comes while they are still like that." The point is that this Ummah is more noble than the rest of the nations, and those brought near within it are more numerous than others and of higher rank, due to the nobility of its religion and the greatness of its Prophet. For this reason it is established by mass transmission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he informed that in this Ummah there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning. In one wording: "With every thousand, seventy thousand," and in another: "With each one, seventy thousand."

The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: "Hisham ibn Marthad [[In H and the rest of the copies: "Yazid", and the correction is from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir.]] al-Tabarani related to us, Muhammad – that is Ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash – related to us, my father related to me, Damdam – meaning Ibn Zur'ah – related to me, from Shurayh – that is Ibn Ubayd – from Abu Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, there will certainly be raised up from among you on the Day of Resurrection a host like the black night, all of them surrounding the earth. The angels will say: What came with Muhammad (ﷺ) is more than what came with the Prophets, peace be upon them.'"[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/297). In its chain is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak and did not hear from his father.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verse 13–26 (part 2 of 3):

It is fitting to mention here [at his saying: "A multitude of the earlier generations, and a few of the later generations" (56:13–14)] the hadith that the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi narrated in "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah" (Proofs of Prophethood), where he said: Abu Nasr ibn Qatadah informed us, Abu 'Amr ibn Matar informed us, Ja'far [i.e., Ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mustafad al-Firyabi] narrated to us: Abu Wahb al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musarrih al-Harrani narrated to me, Sulayman ibn 'Ata' al-Qurashi al-Harrani narrated to us, from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'ah ibn Ribi'i, from Ibn Zaml al-Juhani, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he prayed the dawn prayer, would say, while folding his leg: "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him. I seek the forgiveness of Allah; indeed Allah is ever Accepting of repentance," seventy times. Then he would say: "Seventy times seven hundred. There is no good for one whose sins in a single day exceed seven hundred." He would say that twice, then turn his face towards the people. He liked dreams, and would say: "Has any of you seen anything?" Ibn Zaml said: I said: "I, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Good that you meet, and evil that you avoid, good for us and evil for our enemies, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Relate your dream." I said: I saw all the people upon a wide, easy, level road, and the people were proceeding along the main path. While they were thus, that road rose up over a meadow I had never seen the like of, rippling, its water dripping, containing all kinds of herbage. He said: It was as if I saw the first caravan, when they reached the meadow, glorify Allah, then they made their mounts kneel on the road, and they did not deviate to the right or the left. He said: I seemed to see them proceeding. Then the second caravan came, and they were many times more numerous than them; when they reached the meadow they glorified Allah, then they made their mounts kneel on the road, and among them was the one who grazed and among them was the one who took a handful (of herbage). And they continued thus. He said: Then the great mass of the people came, and when they reached the meadow they glorified Allah and said: "This is the best of abodes." It was as if I saw them inclining right and left. When I saw that, I kept to the road until I reached the far end of the meadow, and there I was, with you, O Messenger of Allah, on a pulpit of seven steps, and you were on its highest step. On your right was a man, wheat-complexioned, straight-haired, aquiline-nosed; when he spoke he rose up, so that he surpassed the men in height. On your left was a man of medium stature, reddish-white, with many moles on his face, as if his hair had been bathed in water; when he spoke you all listened to him with honour. In front of them was an old man most resembling you in form and face; all of you were heading towards him and seeking him. In front of that was a lean she-camel, aged, and you, O Messenger of Allah, seemed to be driving her. He said: The colour of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed for a while, then it passed from him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for what you saw of the smooth, wide, easy road, that is the guidance with which you were carried, and you were upon it. As for the meadow you saw, it is the world and the brightness of its life. I and my companions passed on without clinging to anything of it, and it did not cling to us, and we did not desire it and it did not desire us. Then the second caravan came after us, and they were many times more numerous than us, and among them was the one who grazed and the one who took a handful, and they were saved in that state. Then the great mass of the people came, and they inclined to the right and left in the meadow: Surely to Allah we belong and to Him we return. As for you, you passed on a righteous path, and you will not cease to be upon it until you meet me. As for the pulpit you saw with seven steps, and I upon its highest step, the world is seven thousand years, and I am in its last thousand. As for the man you saw on my right, wheat-complexioned and straight-haired, that is Musa (Moses), peace be upon him; when he speaks he rises above the men by virtue of Allah's speech to him. And the one you saw on my left, of medium stature, reddish-white, with many moles on his face, as if his hair had been bathed in water, that is 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary); we honour him for the honour Allah bestowed upon him. As for the old man you saw most resembling me in form and face, that is our father Ibrahim (Abraham); we all head towards him and follow him. As for the she-camel you saw, and you saw yourself driving her, she is the Hour, which will come upon us. There is no prophet after me, and no community after my community."
He said: After this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not ask anyone about a dream except that a man would come and relate it to him voluntarily.[[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (7/36). Its chain includes Sulayman ibn 'Ata' ibn Qays. Ibn Hibban said in al-Majruhin (1/329): "A shaykh who narrates from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle Abu Mashja'ah ibn Ribi'i, things that are fabricated, not resembling the narrations of the trustworthy; I do not know whether the confusion in them is from him or from Maslamah ibn 'Abd Allah."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿upon thrones woven with gold﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., interwoven (marmulah) with gold, meaning woven with it. Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others said likewise.
Al-Suddi said: interwoven with gold and pearls. 'Ikrimah said: latticed with pearls and rubies. Ibn Jarir said: from this is named the girth (wadin) of the she-camel that goes under her belly; it is fa'il in the sense of maf'ul, because it is plaited; and likewise the thrones in Paradise are plaited with gold and pearls.
And He said: ﴿reclining upon them, facing one another﴾, i.e., faces towards one another, none of them behind another. ﴿There will circulate among them youths made eternal﴾, i.e., they are made eternal in one state, they do not age from it, nor grow grey, nor change. ﴿With cups, and jugs, and a cup from a flowing spring﴾. As for al-akwab, they are the vessels without spouts or handles. The abariq are those that combine both descriptions. The ku'us are the goblets. All of it is from wine flowing from a running spring (ma'in), not from containers that run out and are emptied, but from flowing springs.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will not be affected with headache thereby, nor will they be intoxicated﴾, i.e., their heads will not ache and their intellects will not be taken away; rather it remains constant along with the exhilarating potency and the pleasure attained.
Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: in wine there are four qualities: intoxication, headache, vomiting, and urination. Allah mentioned the wine of Paradise and freed it from these qualities.
Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Atiyyah, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: ﴿They will not be affected with headache thereby﴾ means: there is no headache of the head for them therein.
And regarding His saying ﴿nor will they be intoxicated﴾ they said: i.e., it does not take away their intellects.

* *

His saying: ﴿And fruit of what they choose, and the flesh of birds of what they desire﴾, i.e., they will be served with fruits of whatever they choose from among the produce.
This verse is evidence for the permissibility of eating fruit in the manner of choosing it, and the hadith of "Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb" supports this, which the hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in his Musnad: al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Narsi narrated to us, al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sawiyyah narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ikrash narrated to us, from his father Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb, who said: The Banu Murrah sent me with their zakat of property to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I came to Madinah and found him sitting among the Muhajirun and the Ansar. I came to him with camels like the roots of the arta-tree. He said: "Who is the man?" I said: Ikrash ibn Dhu'ayb. He said: "Raise (your lineage) in genealogy," so I traced my lineage to "Murrah ibn 'Ubayd," and this is the zakat of "Murrah ibn 'Ubayd." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "These are the camels of my people, these are the zakat of my people." Then he ordered that they be branded with the brand of the zakat camels and added to them. Then he took my hand and we went to the house of Umm Salamah, and he said: "Is there any food?" We were brought a bowl abundant with thareed and wadhar, and he began to eat from it. I began to reach with my hand around its edges, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seized my right hand with his left hand and said: "O Ikrash, eat from one place, for it is one kind of food." Then we were brought a tray containing dates, or fresh dates—'Ubayd Allah was unsure whether it was fresh dates or dried dates—and I began to eat from in front of me, and the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) moved about the tray, and he said: "O Ikrash, eat from wherever you wish, for it is not one colour." Then water was brought, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) washed his hand, and wiped with the moisture of his palms his face, his forearms and his head three times, then said: "O Ikrash, this is the ablution from what fire has changed."
Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it at length, and Ibn Majah narrated it in full, both from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Abu al-Hudhayl al-'Ala' ibn al-Fadl, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1848) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3274). 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ikrash has been criticised, and this hadith of his has been criticised. Al-Bukhari said: "His hadith is not established." Al-'Uqayli reported from him that he said: "There is a problem (nazar) in its chain."]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib (strange); we do not know it except from his narration."

Imam Ahmad said: Bahz ibn Asad and 'Affan narrated to us—and al-hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Shaybān narrated to us—they said: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us, who said: Anas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) liked dreams, and whenever a man saw a dream he would ask about it if he did not know him; but if a well-known person praised him, he was more pleased with his dream. A woman came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw as if I was brought out of Madinah and was admitted to Paradise, and I heard a thud, to which Paradise trembled, and I looked, and there was so-and-so son of so-and-so, and so-and-so son of so-and-so," and she named twelve men whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had sent as a detachment before that. They were brought, wearing tattered garments, their veins flowing with blood. It was said: "Take them to the river al-Baydakh" or "al-Baydhakh." He said: They were dipped in it, and they came out with faces like the full moon. Then they were brought a golden dish containing dates, and they ate from its dates whatever they wished, and whichever way they turned it they ate whatever fruit they desired, and I ate with them. Then the messenger came from that detachment and said: "Our affair was such-and-such, and so-and-so and so-and-so were struck," until he counted twelve men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the woman and said: "Relate your dream," and she related it, and kept saying: "Then so-and-so and so-and-so were brought, just as he said."
This is the wording of Abu Ya'la. The hafiz al-Diya' said: this is upon the condition of Muslim.[[al-Musnad of Imam Ahmad (3/135); Musnad Abi Ya'la no. (3289), (6/44). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/175): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

The hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated to us, Rayhan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn Mansur, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when a man plucks a fruit in Paradise, another grows in its place."[[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/102). In its chain is 'Abbad, who has been criticised.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿and the flesh of birds﴾. Imam Ahmad said:

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verse 13–26 (part 3 of 3):

Sayyar ibn Hatim narrated to us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the birds of Paradise are like the Bukht camels (a large breed of camel), grazing in the trees of Paradise." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed these are soft, pampered birds!" He said: "The one who eats them is more pampered than they are," saying it three times, "and I hope that you will be among those who eat from them." Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. [Al-Musnad (3/221).]

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Maqdisi related in his book "Sifat al-Jannah" from the hadith of Isma'il ibn 'Ali al-Khutabi, from Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Khuyuti, from 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn 'Asim, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ziyad, from Zur'ah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: Ṭūbā (a tree in Paradise) was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Bakr, has it reached you what Ṭūbā is?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Ṭūbā is a tree in Paradise. No one knows its length except Allah. A rider would travel for seventy autumns under one of its branches. Its leaves are ḥulal (robes), and birds settle upon it like the Bukht camels." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there indeed a pampered bird there?" He said: "The one who eats it is more pampered than it, and you are among them, if Allah wills." [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as cited in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/649).]

Qatadah said, regarding His saying ﴿and the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire﴾: It was mentioned to us that Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see its birds are pampered just as its people are pampered." He said: "The one who eats them, by Allah, O Abu Bakr, is more pampered than them. Indeed they are like the Bukht camels, and I expect from Allah that you will eat from them, O Abu Bakr." [This is mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain), though it has also been transmitted through al-Hasan, likewise mursal, narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (12/13).]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to me, Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated to us, the son of my brother Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about al-Kawthar. He said: "It is a river that my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has given me in Paradise, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. In it are birds whose necks are like the necks of jazur (slaughtered animals)." 'Umar said: "Indeed they are pampered!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The one who eats them is more pampered than they are."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from al-Qa'nabi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from his father, from Anas, and said: "Hasan" (good). [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2542, where he said: "hasan gharib" (good, strange).]
