He said: 'This is your brother Musa ibn Imran and those who follow him from the Children of Israel.' I said: 'My Lord, then where is my nation?' He said: 'Look to your right, toward the mountain passes.' Then I saw the faces of men." He said: "He said: 'Are you pleased?' I said: 'I am pleased, my Lord.' He said: 'Look to the horizon on your left,' and then I saw the faces of men. He said: 'Are you pleased?' I said: 'I am pleased, my Lord.' He said: 'Indeed, with these there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning.'" He said: Ukkashah ibn Mihsan of the Banu Asad, (Sa'id said: and he was a veteran of Badr), stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them." He said: "He said: 'O Allah, make him one of them.'" Then another man stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them." He said: "Ukkashah has preceded you with this." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you are able—may my father and mother be your ransom—to be among the companions of the seventy thousand, then do so; otherwise, be among the companions of the mountain passes; otherwise, be among the companions of the horizon. For I have seen many people gathered around him (in a crowd)." Then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar". Then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar". He said: "I truly hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar". Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿A company of the earlier generations, and a company of the later ones﴾. He said: So we said among ourselves: Who are these seventy thousand? We said: They are those who were born in Islam and did not associate partners with Allah. He said: This reached him, and he said: "Rather, they are those who do not seek cauterization, do not seek incantation, and do not believe in omens, and upon their Lord they rely."

Similarly, Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it from Qatadah through two other chains, with similar wording. This hadith has many other routes outside this chain in the sound (sahih) collections and others.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding: ﴿A company of the earlier generations, and a company of the later ones﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both of them are from my nation."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verses 27–40 (part 1 of 4):

When God mentioned the final destiny of the foremost (al-sabiqun), who are the muqarrabun (those brought near), He followed it with the mention of the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), who are the righteous (al-abrar), as Maymun ibn Mihran said: "The companions of the right are a rank below the muqarrabun." So He said: ﴿And the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ That is: What are the companions of the right hand? What is their condition? And what is their final destiny? Then He explained this by saying: ﴿Among lote trees without thorns.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu al-Ahwas, Qatadah ibn Salamah, al-Saffar ibn Nusayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Abdullah ibn Kathir, al-Suddi, Abu Hamzah, and others said: it is the one without thorns. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the one laden with fruit, and this is a report from 'Ikrimah and Mujahid. Qatadah also said likewise: "We used to be told that it is the one laden with fruit that has no thorns."

The apparent meaning is that both are intended. The lote tree of this world has many thorns and little fruit, whereas in the Hereafter it is the reverse: it has no thorns, and it has abundant fruit that weighs down its branches, as the memorizer of hadith (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr ibn Salman al-Najjad said.

Muhammad ibn Muhammad, namely al-Baghawi, told us: Hamzah ibn 'Abbas told me: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman told us: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us: Safwan ibn 'Amr informed us, from Sulaym ibn 'Amir, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "God benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions." He said: A Bedouin came one day and said: "O Messenger of God, has God mentioned in Paradise a tree that harms its companion?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "And what is it?" He said: "The lote tree, for it has harmful thorns." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Does God not say: ﴿Among lote trees without thorns⦆? God has cut off its thorns and placed in the position of each thorn a fruit. Indeed, it brings forth fruit from which each fruit splits open to reveal seventy-two kinds of food, no two of which resemble each other."

Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us: Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak told us: Yahya ibn Hamzah told us: Thawr ibn Yazid told me: Habib ibn 'Ubayd told me, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when a Bedouin came and said: "O Messenger of God, I hear you mention a tree in Paradise, and I know of no tree with more thorns than it," meaning the talh (acacia). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God will place in the position of each of its thorns a fruit like the testicle of a castrated he-goat, and in it there will be seventy kinds of food, no one of which resembles another."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And acacia trees with layered fruit.﴾ Talh: these are large trees found in the land of the Hijaz, from among the 'idah trees. Its singular is talhah, and it is a tree with many thorns. Ibn Jarir cited a verse by one of the camel-drivers (hudah):

"Their guide gave them good news and said:
'Tomorrow you will see the acacias and the mountains...'"

Mujahid said: ﴿Layered﴾ means with fruit piled up upon one another, reminding the Quraysh of this, for they used to marvel at the wajj (a tree) and its shade of talh and sidr.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿Layered﴾ means arranged in rows. Ibn 'Abbas said: it resembles the talh of this world, but it has fruit sweeter than honey.

Al-Jawhari said: talh is a dialectal variant of talh (the spathe/flower cluster of the palm), in the sense of talh.

I say: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from a shaykh of Hamdan, who said: I heard 'Ali say: "This word in ﴿and acacia layered⦆ is read as talʿ manḍud (layered spathes)." According to this, the phrase would be a description of the sidr: He described it as being without thorns (makhdud), and its spathes (talʿ) as layered (manḍud), meaning abundance of fruit. And God knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj told us: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from Idris, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, regarding ﴿and acacia layered⦆, who said: "The banana." He said: It has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, Qusamah ibn Zuhayr, Qatadah, and Abu Hazrah, the same. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd also said this, and Ibn Zayd added: "The people of Yemen call the banana talh." Ibn Jarir mentioned only this view.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And extended shade.﴾ Al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah told us: Sufyan told us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆"

Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'raj, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us: Fulayh told us, from Hilal ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆"

Al-Bukhari also narrated it likewise from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Fulayh with this wording. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah. And al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated it from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah. And 'Awf narrated it from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Hajjaj told us, both saying: Shu'bah told us: I heard Abu al-Dahhak narrate from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel seventy or a hundred years. It is the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld)."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God, who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆"

Its chain is good, though they did not record it. Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise from Abu Kurayb, from 'Abdah and 'Abd al-Rahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, with the same wording. al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us: Mihran told us: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid told us, from Ziyad, the client of Banu Makhzum, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆" When this reached Ka'b, he said: "He spoke the truth. By Him who sent down the Torah to Musa and the Furqan to Muhammad, if a man were to ride a four-year-old (haqqah) or a young camel (jadha'ah) and circle around the base of that tree, he would not reach its end until he collapsed from old age. God planted it with His own hand and breathed into it of His spirit. Its branches extend beyond the wall of Paradise, and there is no river in Paradise except that it flows out from the root of that tree."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Minhal al-Darir told us: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ told us, from Sa'd ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it."

Al-Bukhari likewise narrated it from Rawh ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min, from Yazid ibn Zurayʿ. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it likewise from 'Imran ibn Dawar al-Qattan, from Qatadah with this wording. Ma'mar and Abu Hilal also narrated it from Qatadah with the same wording. Al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Sahl ibn Sa'd, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "In Paradise there is a tree that a swift, well-trained, galloping horseman could ride for a hundred years without crossing it."

This is an established hadith from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), indeed mutawatir, whose authenticity is firmly affirmed by the critical scholars of hadith, because of the multiplicity of its chains, the strength of its isnads, and the reliability of its narrators.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Bakr told us: Abu Husayn told us, saying: "We were at a gate in a certain place, and with us were Abu Salih and Shaqiq (meaning al-Dabbi). Abu Salih narrated, saying: Abu Hurayrah told me: 'In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for seventy years.'" Abu Salih said: "Do you call Abu Hurayrah a liar?" He replied: "I do not call Abu Hurayrah a liar, but I call you a liar." This displeased the reciters (qurra') on that day.

I say: Whoever denies this hadith has refuted himself, despite its being established, authentic, and traced back to the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj told us: Ziyad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Furat al-Qazzaz told us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "There is no tree in Paradise except that its trunk is of gold." Then he said: "Hasan gharib."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' told us: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi told us, from Zam'ah ibn Salih, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The extended shade is a tree in Paradise upon a trunk, whose shade is such that a rider would travel in its surroundings for a hundred years. The people of Paradise will go out to it, the people of the upper chambers (ghurraf) and others, and they will converse in its shade. Some of them will desire and mention the amusements of this world, and God will send a wind from Paradise, and that tree will move with every amusement of this world."

This is a strange report (athar gharib), and its chain is good, strong, and sound.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj told us: Ibn Yamani told us: Sufyan told us: Abu Ishaq told us, from 'Amr ibn Maymun concerning His words: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "Seventy thousand years." Ibn Jarir likewise narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, the same. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "Five hundred thousand years."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us: Husayn ibn Nafi' told us, from al-Hasan concerning the words of God Most High: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it."

'Awf said, from al-Hasan: "It has reached me that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it.'" Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn 'Abbas said, from 'Ikrimah, by way of Shabib: "In Paradise there is a tree that bears no fruit, under which one may shelter." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Abu Hazra said, concerning His words ﴿and extended shade﴾, that it does not cease, and that there is in it neither sun nor heat, like the time before the break of dawn.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Paradise is sajsaj (a mild, temperate state), like the time between the break of dawn and sunrise."

The verses have already preceded, such as His words ﴿And We will admit them to shade, deep shade﴾ [An-Nisa 4:57], His words ﴿Its food is constant and its shade﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 13:35], His words ﴿In shades and springs﴾ [Al-Mursalat 77:41], and others besides these.

* *

As for His words ﴿and flowing water﴾, al-Thawri said: [meaning] it flows without a trench.

The discussion has already taken place at the explanation of His words ﴿therein are rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad 47:15], with what makes repeating it here unnecessary.

* *

As for His words ﴿and abundant fruit, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, this means that they have abundant fruits, varied in colours, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit, they say: "This is what we were provided with before," and they are brought it in resemblance﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:25], meaning that the form resembles the form, but the taste is not the same taste.

In the two Sahihs, concerning the mention of the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), he said: "Its leaves are like the ears of elephants, and its fruits like the large jars of Hajar."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3207) and Sahih Muslim no. (162), from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Also in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Malik, from Zayd, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The sun eclipsed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed, and the people prayed with him," and he mentioned the prayer. In it: they said, "O Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something in this place of yours, then we saw you draw back." He said: "I saw Paradise, and I took from it a cluster. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world endures."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1052) and Sahih Muslim no. (907).]]

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: Abu Khaythama narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, Ibn 'Aqil narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: "While we were in the Zuhr prayer, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) advanced, so we advanced with him. Then he reached for something to take it, then he drew back. When he finished the prayer, Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you did something today in the prayer that you did not do before?' He said: 'Paradise was shown to me, with what it contains of splendour and radiance. I reached for a bunch of grapes to bring it to you, but it was kept from me. Had I brought it to you, you would have eaten from it for as long as heaven and earth endure, and it would not have diminished.'"[[The hadith was previously cited at the commentary on verse 35 of Surah al-Ra'd.]]

Muslim narrated, from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, something similar.[[The hadith has been cited in the previous place.]]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn Bahr narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from 'Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, that he heard 'Utba ibn 'Abd al-Sulami say: "A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about the Basin (al-Hawd), and he mentioned Paradise. Then the Bedouin said: 'Does it contain fruit?' He said: 'Yes, and in it is a tree called Tuba.'" He mentioned something I do not remember. He said: "What tree of our land does it resemble?" He said: "It does not resemble any tree of your land." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Have you come to al-Sham?" He said: "No." He said: "It resembles a tree in al-Sham called al-Jawza (the walnut), which grows on a single trunk, and its top spreads out." He said: "How large is its base?" He said: "If a young camel of your family's camels were to travel, it would not encircle its base until its neck was broken from old age." He said: "Does it have grapes?" He said: "Yes." He said: "How large is the cluster?" He said: "It is a month's journey for the speckled crow, and it never tires." He said: "How large is the grape?" He said: "Has your father ever slaughtered a billy goat of his flock that was very large?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he skinned its hide and gave it to your mother, and said: 'Make us a bucket from it?'" He said: "Yes." The Bedouin said: "Would that grape satisfy me and the people of my household?" He said: "Yes, and most of your clan."[[Al-Musnad (4/184).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿lā maqṭū'a wa lā mamnū'a﴾ (neither cut off nor forbidden), this means: they are not cut off in winter or in summer, but their fruit is constant and perpetual forever. Whenever they seek it, they find it. Nothing is withheld from them, by the power of Allah.

Qatada said: "No branch, no thorn and no distance prevents them from taking it." It has already been mentioned in the hadith: "When a man reaches for a fruit, another one returns in its place."

* *

As for His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, this means: high, soft and luxurious.

Al-Nasa'i and Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Their height is as between the heaven and the earth, and the distance between them is five hundred years."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2540). In it appears: "This is a hadith gharib (unusual, singly transmitted) which we do not know," and the word "hasan" is not in it, and likewise it appears in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib (sound but singly transmitted) hadith which we do not know except from the hadith of Rishdin ibn Sa'd." He said: "Some scholars said: the meaning of this hadith is the height of the couches in the ranks, and the distance between two ranks is as between the heaven and the earth."

Thus he (al-Tirmidhi) said that he does not know this except through the narration of Rishdin ibn Sa'd, who is the Egyptian, and he is weak. Likewise Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Rishdin.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/106).]] Then he (al-Tabari) and Ibn Abi Hatim both narrated it, both from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, and he mentioned it. Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Nu'aym ibn Hammad, from Ibn Wahb. Al-Diya' (al-Maqdisi) also transmitted it in Sifat al-Jannah, from the hadith of Harmala, from Ibn Wahb, with the like of it. Imam Ahmad narrated it from Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'a, who said: Darraj narrated to us, and he mentioned it.[[Al-Musnad (3/75).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from Abu Sahl (meaning Kathir ibn Ziyad), from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "The height of a man's couch among the people of Paradise is an eighty-year journey."

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, We created them with a [special] creation. And We made them virgins, loving, equal in age, for the companions of the right﴾, the pronoun refers to something not previously mentioned. But since the context indicates it, namely the mention of the couches, [it refers to] the women who recline upon them, that mention is sufficient and the pronoun returns to them. This is like His words: ﴿When there were displayed before him, in the evening, the swift steeds. He said: "Indeed, I have loved the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord," until they were hidden behind the veil﴾ [Sad 38:31-32], meaning the sun, according to the well-known view of the commentators.

Al-Akhfash said, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation﴾: he concealed them (the pronoun) and did not mention them before. Abu 'Ubayda said: they were mentioned in His words ﴿And [there are] wide-eyed maidens, like hidden pearls﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 56:22-23].

So His words ﴿Indeed, We created them﴾ mean: We restored them in the Hereafter's creation, after they had been old women with weak eyes and grey hair. They became virgins, loving (ʿuruban), that is, after being previously married they returned as virgins, loving (ʿuruban), that is, endearing to their husbands with sweetness, grace and beauty.[[In MS A: "ma kan 'ijaf rumsa" (they had been old, weak-eyed women).]]

Some said: ʿuruban means "playful and coquettish."

Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi narrated from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation﴾: "They are old women who were in the world, weak-eyed and with sore eyelids." Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib (singly transmitted), and Musa and Yazid are weak."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3296) and Tafsir al-Tabari (27/107).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Himsi narrated to us, Adam (meaning Ibn Abi Iyas) narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Jabir, from Yazid ibn Murra, from Salama ibn Yazid, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation﴾: meaning the previously married women and the virgins who were in the world."[[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/40) and Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah no. (389), through the chain of Shaybān. Jabir ibn Yazid is weak.]]

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadala narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: "An old woman came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah that He admit me to Paradise.' He said: 'O mother of so-and-so, indeed Paradise is not entered by an old woman.' She turned away weeping. He said: 'Inform her that she will not enter it while she is old, for Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation. And We made them virgins﴾.'"

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise in al-Shama'il from 'Abd ibn Humayd.[[Al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyya of al-Tirmidhi no. (230).]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Hashim al-Bayruti narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abi Karima narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salama, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me about Allah's words ﴿And [there are] wide-eyed maidens﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 56:22].' He said: 'Hur (wide-eyed): white. 'In (large-eyed): large of eyes; the eyelashes of the hawra' are like the wing of an eagle.' I said: 'Inform me about His words ﴿like hidden pearls﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 56:23].' He said: 'Their clearness is the clearness of the pearl that is in the shells, which no hand has touched.' I said: 'Inform me about His words ﴿therein are good and beautiful [women]﴾ [Al-Rahman 55:70].' He said: 'Good in character, beautiful in face.' I said: 'Inform me about His words ﴿as if they were hidden eggs﴾ [Al-Saffat 37:49].' He said: 'Their delicacy is like the delicacy of the membrane which you see inside the eggshell next to the shell, which is al-ghirqi'.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me about His words ﴿loving, equal in age﴾.' He said: 'They are those who were taken in the abode of this world as old women, grey-haired and with sore eyes. Allah created them after old age, and made them virgins, loving, passionate, endearing, equal in age, of one birth.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, are the women of this world better, or the wide-eyed maidens?' He said: 'Rather, the women of this world are better than the wide-eyed maidens, as the outer garment is better than the lining.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why is that?' He said: 'Because of their prayers, their fasting, and their worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah clothes their faces in light and their bodies in silk, white of colour, green of garments, yellow of ornaments. Their censers are of pearls, and their combs of gold. They say: "We are the eternal, so we never die. We are the joyful, so we are never miserable. We are the ones who remain, so we never depart. Indeed, we are the content, so we are never displeased. Blessed is the one for whom we are, and who is for us." ' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a woman among us marries two husbands, or three, or four, then dies and enters Paradise, and they enter with her. Who will be her husband?' He said: 'O Umm Salama, she will be given the choice, and she will choose the one with the best character. She will say: "O Lord, this one was the best in character with me, so marry me to him." O Umm Salama, good character has departed with the good of this world and the Hereafter.'"[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/368). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/119): "In it is Isma'il ibn Abi Karima, whom Abu Hatim and Ibn 'Adi declared weak." In MS A: "O Umm Sulaym."]]

And in the long and well-known hadith of the Trumpet [[The hadith of the Trumpet has already been mentioned in the commentary on verse 73 of Surat al-An'am.]] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will intercede for all the believers to enter Paradise. Allah will say: "I have granted you intercession, and I have permitted them to enter it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "By He who sent me with the truth, you are not more knowing in the world of your wives and your dwellings than the people of Paradise are of their wives and their dwellings. A man among them will enter upon seventy-two wives: seventy whom Allah has created, and two from the offspring of Adam, who are superior to those whom Allah has created because of their worship of Allah in the world. He enters upon the first of them in a chamber of ruby, upon a throne of gold studded with pearls, on which are seventy mattresses of silk and brocade. He places his hand between her shoulders, then looks at his hand from her chest through her garments, her skin and her flesh, and he can see the marrow of her shin as you see the thread in a ruby tube. Her liver is a mirror for him, and his liver is a mirror for her. While he is with her, he does not tire of her and she does not tire of him, and each time he comes to her he finds her a virgin. His member does not slacken, and she does not complain of her private parts, except that there is no semen and no menstruation. While he is in this state, he is called: 'We have known that you do not tire and are not tired, but you have other wives besides her.' So he goes out and comes to them one by one, and each time he comes to one, she says: 'By Allah, there is nothing in Paradise better than you, and nothing in Paradise more beloved to me than you.'"

Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Hurairah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said to him: "Shall we have intercourse in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, with vigorous intercourse. When he rises from her, she returns pure and a virgin again." [[Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 2633 (Mawarid), and Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 393, through Ibn Wahb. Darraj is criticised (mutakallam fihi).]]

Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Jabir al-Faqih al-Baghdadi narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Daqiq al-Wasiti narrated to us; Mu'alla ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti narrated to us; Sharik narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the people of Paradise have intercourse with their wives, they return as virgins." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/91). In it is Mu'alla ibn Abd al-Rahman, who is a liar (kadhdhab).]]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The believer in Paradise will be given the strength of such-and-such in regard to women." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will he be able to bear that?" He said: "He will be given the strength of a hundred."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud, and said: "Sahih, gharib." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 2012, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2536.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi, from Za'idah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurairah, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we reach our wives in Paradise?" He said: "A man reaches a hundred virgins in a single day." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (2/12, 13).]]

The Hafiz Abu Abd Allah al-Maqdisi said: "This hadith, in my view, meets the conditions of the Sahih, and Allah knows best."

* *

His saying: ﴿ʿUruban﴾ (loving, devoted to their husbands). Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas: it means "those who make themselves beloved to their husbands." Do you not see the she-camel that is ḍubʿah (playful and coquettish)? She is like that.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas: "al-ʿUrub" are those who are passionate about their husbands, and their husbands are passionate about them. Likewise said Abd Allah ibn Sarjis, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu al-Aliyah, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, Atiyyah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

Thawr ibn Zayd narrated from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying ﴿ʿUruban﴾, and he said: "She is one who is coquettish with her husband (al-Milqah)."

Shu'bah narrated from Simak, from Ikrimah: "She is al-Ghanijah (one who is alluring and flirtatious)."

Al-Ajlah ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ikrimah: "She is al-Shakilah (one who is graceful in gesture)."

Salih ibn Hayyan narrated from Abd Allah ibn Buraydah concerning His saying ﴿ʿUruban﴾: "Al-Shikilah in the dialect of the people of Makkah, and al-Ghanijah in the dialect of the people of Madinah."

Tamim ibn Hadhlam said: "It is the goodness of conduct toward the husband (husn al-tabaʿʿul)."

Zayd ibn Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman said: "Al-ʿUrub: the fine speech."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Sahl ibn Uthman al-Askari: Abu Ali narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, concerning ﴿ʿUruban﴾: "Their speech is Arabic." [[Note: the isnad here is as found in the text.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Atraban﴾ (of equal age). Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas: it means "of one age, thirty-three years."

Mujahid said: "Al-Atrab are those who are equal (al-mustawiyat)." In another report from him: "the similar ones." Atiyyah said: "the peers." Al-Suddi said: ﴿Atraban﴾ means: "in character, those who are bound in affection among themselves, with no hatred or envy among them, i.e., not like co-wives who were enemies in the world."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from Abd Allah ibn al-Kahf, from al-Hasan and Muhammad, concerning ﴿ʿUruban Atraban﴾, they said: "Those equal in age, who are in harmony together and play together."

Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a gathering place for the ḥūr ʿīn (wide-eyed, lovely maidens), who raise their voices with sounds never heard by creation. They say: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall never perish; we are the ones who live in bliss, so we shall never be miserable; we are the ones who are content, so we shall never be wrathful. Happy is he who is for us and we are for him.'" Then he said: "This is a hadith gharib."

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us; Isma'il ibn Umar narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from a certain Abd Allah ibn Rafi', from one of the sons of Anas ibn Malik, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The ḥūr ʿīn will sing in Paradise, saying: 'We are good and beautiful; we have been kept for noble husbands.'" [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Matalib al-ʿAliyah (4/402) and attributed it to Abu Ya'la; the editor quoted al-Busayri: "Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in it is a narrator who is unnamed." Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 254, by the same route.]]

I say: This Isma'il ibn Umar is Abu al-Mundhir al-Wasiti, one of the trustworthy and firm narrators. The Imam Abd al-Rahim ibn Ibrahim, known as Duhaym, also narrated this hadith, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Awn ibn al-Khattab ibn Abd Allah ibn Rafi', from a son of Anas, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The ḥūr ʿīn sing in Paradise: 'We are the fine companions, created for noble husbands.'" [[Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 432, through Duhaym; by al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th, no. 420, through Ibn Abd al-Hakam; and by Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Ba'th, no. 75, through Kathir ibn Ubayd, all through Ibn Abi Fudayk. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, no. 4887, through al-Hasan ibn Dawud, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Awn ibn al-Khattab, from Anas, similarly. Al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (4/226): "Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Tabarani narrated it, and its isnad is close (to sound). Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from a son of Anas who was not named, from Anas." Al-Bukhari pointed to a difference of opinion regarding it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (7/16).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿li-Ashab al-Yamin﴾ (for the companions of the right hand). That is: "We created them for the companions of the right hand," or "They were stored up for the companions of the right hand," or "They were wedded to the companions of the right hand." The most apparent view is that it is connected to His saying: ﴿Indeed We created them with a special creation. And We made them virgins, loving, of equal age, for the companions of the right hand﴾; so the meaning is: "We created them for the companions of the right hand." This is the interpretation of Ibn Jarir. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/109).]]

It is related from Abu Sulayman al-Darani, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: "I prayed one night, then sat making supplication. The cold was severe, so I began to supplicate with one hand, and sleep overcame me, and I slept. I saw a ḥūrāʾ (maiden) the like of whom had never been seen, and she was saying: 'O Abu Sulayman, do you supplicate with one hand while I am being nourished for you in bliss for five hundred years!'"

I say: It is possible that His saying ﴿li-Ashab al-Yamin﴾ is connected to what precedes it, namely His saying ﴿Atraban li-Ashab al-Yamin﴾, meaning: "of equal age among them," as came in the hadith which al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, from the hadith of Jarir, from Umarah ibn al-Qaqa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first company to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon; those who follow them will be on the brightness of the most brilliant star in the sky. They will not urinate or defecate, nor spit or blow their noses. Their combs are of gold, their perspiration is musk, their censers are of aloes wood, and their wives are the ḥūr ʿīn. Their character is that of one man, in the form of their father Adam, sixty cubits tall." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3327, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2834.]]

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun and Affan narrated to us, both saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, and al-Tabarani narrated it, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise naked, beardless, with white skin, curly hair, and kohl-darkened eyes, being thirty or thirty-three years old, and they will be on the form of Adam, sixty cubits tall, with a breadth of seven cubits." [[Al-Musnad (2/295) and al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 4894.]]

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Imran al-Qattan, from Qatadah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise naked, beardless, kohl-eyed, being thirty or thirty-three years old." Then he said: "Hasan gharib." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2545.]]

Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever dies among the people of Paradise, young or old, will be returned at the age of thirty-three in Paradise, and they will never exceed that age. Likewise the people of the Fire."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Rishdin ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2562, narrated from the route of Ibn Wahb; and Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 259.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: al-Qasim ibn Hashim narrated to us; Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us; Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah al-Asqalani narrated to us; al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Harun ibn Ri'ab, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise upon the stature of Adam, sixty cubits by the cubit of the King, with the beauty of Yusuf, and with the age of Isa at thirty-three years, and upon the tongue of Muhammad, with smooth, beardless, kohl-eyed faces." [[Sifat al-Jannah by Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. 215.]]

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Mahmud ibn Khalid and Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to us, both saying: Umar narrated to us from al-Awza'i, from Harun ibn Ri'ab, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise will be raised (in another reading, 'will enter') upon the form of Adam, at the age of thirty-three, beardless and without body hair, with kohl-lined eyes. Then they will be taken to a tree in Paradise, and they will be clothed from it. Their garments will not wear out, and their youth will not fade."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿A company of the earlier generations, and a company of the later ones﴾, meaning: a group from the first (generations) and a group from the last (generations).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bakkar narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, (he said: some of them used to take from others), who said: We stayed up one night with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then we went to him in the morning, and he said: "The prophets and their followers were shown to me with their nations. A prophet would pass by me with a small group, a prophet with three, and a prophet with no one with him." Qatadah recited this verse: ﴿Is there not among you a man of right judgment?﴾ [Hud: 78]. He said: "Then Musa ibn Imran passed by me with a great multitude of the Children of Israel." He said: "I said: 'My Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is your brother Musa ibn Imran and those who follow him from the Children of Israel.' I said: 'My Lord, then where is my nation?' He said: 'Look to your right, toward the mountain passes.' Then I saw the faces of men." He said: "He said: 'Are you pleased?' I said: 'I am pleased, my Lord.' He said: 'Look to the horizon on your left,' and then I saw the faces of men. He said: 'Are you pleased?' I said: 'I am pleased, my Lord.' He said: 'Indeed, with these there are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning.'" He said: Ukkashah ibn Mihsan of the Banu Asad, (Sa'id said: and he was a veteran of Badr), stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them." He said: "He said: 'O Allah, make him one of them.'" Then another man stood up and said: "O Prophet of Allah, ask Allah to make me one of them." He said: "Ukkashah has preceded you with this." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you are able—may my father and mother be your ransom—to be among the companions of the seventy thousand, then do so; otherwise, be among the companions of the mountain passes; otherwise, be among the companions of the horizon. For I have seen many people gathered around him (in a crowd)." Then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise." So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar". Then he said: "I truly hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar". He said: "I truly hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise." He said: So we exclaimed "Allahu Akbar". Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿A company of the earlier generations, and a company of the later ones﴾. He said: So we said among ourselves: Who are these seventy thousand? We said: They are those who were born in Islam and did not associate partners with Allah. He said: This reached him, and he said: "Rather, they are those who do not seek cauterization, do not seek incantation, and do not believe in omens, and upon their Lord they rely."

Similarly, Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it from Qatadah through two other chains, with similar wording. This hadith has many other routes outside this chain in the sound (sahih) collections and others.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding: ﴿A company of the earlier generations, and a company of the later ones﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both of them are from my nation."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verses 27–40 (part 1 of 4):

When God mentioned the final destiny of the foremost (al-sabiqun), who are the muqarrabun (those brought near), He followed it with the mention of the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), who are the righteous (al-abrar), as Maymun ibn Mihran said: "The companions of the right are a rank below the muqarrabun." So He said: ﴿And the companions of the right hand, what are the companions of the right hand?﴾ That is: What are the companions of the right hand? What is their condition? And what is their final destiny? Then He explained this by saying: ﴿Among lote trees without thorns.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, Abu al-Ahwas, Qatadah ibn Salamah, al-Saffar ibn Nusayr, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Abdullah ibn Kathir, al-Suddi, Abu Hamzah, and others said: it is the one without thorns. It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the one laden with fruit, and this is a report from 'Ikrimah and Mujahid. Qatadah also said likewise: "We used to be told that it is the one laden with fruit that has no thorns."

The apparent meaning is that both are intended. The lote tree of this world has many thorns and little fruit, whereas in the Hereafter it is the reverse: it has no thorns, and it has abundant fruit that weighs down its branches, as the memorizer of hadith (al-Hafiz) Abu Bakr ibn Salman al-Najjad said.

Muhammad ibn Muhammad, namely al-Baghawi, told us: Hamzah ibn 'Abbas told me: 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman told us: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us: Safwan ibn 'Amr informed us, from Sulaym ibn 'Amir, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "God benefits us through the Bedouins and their questions." He said: A Bedouin came one day and said: "O Messenger of God, has God mentioned in Paradise a tree that harms its companion?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "And what is it?" He said: "The lote tree, for it has harmful thorns." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Does God not say: ﴿Among lote trees without thorns⦆? God has cut off its thorns and placed in the position of each thorn a fruit. Indeed, it brings forth fruit from which each fruit splits open to reveal seventy-two kinds of food, no two of which resemble each other."

Another chain: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud said: Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us: Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak told us: Yahya ibn Hamzah told us: Thawr ibn Yazid told me: Habib ibn 'Ubayd told me, from 'Utbah ibn 'Abd al-Sulami, who said: I was sitting with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when a Bedouin came and said: "O Messenger of God, I hear you mention a tree in Paradise, and I know of no tree with more thorns than it," meaning the talh (acacia). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God will place in the position of each of its thorns a fruit like the testicle of a castrated he-goat, and in it there will be seventy kinds of food, no one of which resembles another."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And acacia trees with layered fruit.﴾ Talh: these are large trees found in the land of the Hijaz, from among the 'idah trees. Its singular is talhah, and it is a tree with many thorns. Ibn Jarir cited a verse by one of the camel-drivers (hudah):

"Their guide gave them good news and said:
'Tomorrow you will see the acacias and the mountains...'"

Mujahid said: ﴿Layered﴾ means with fruit piled up upon one another, reminding the Quraysh of this, for they used to marvel at the wajj (a tree) and its shade of talh and sidr.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿Layered﴾ means arranged in rows. Ibn 'Abbas said: it resembles the talh of this world, but it has fruit sweeter than honey.

Al-Jawhari said: talh is a dialectal variant of talh (the spathe/flower cluster of the palm), in the sense of talh.

I say: Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from a shaykh of Hamdan, who said: I heard 'Ali say: "This word in ﴿and acacia layered⦆ is read as talʿ manḍud (layered spathes)." According to this, the phrase would be a description of the sidr: He described it as being without thorns (makhdud), and its spathes (talʿ) as layered (manḍud), meaning abundance of fruit. And God knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj told us: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from Idris, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, regarding ﴿and acacia layered⦆, who said: "The banana." He said: It has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, Qusamah ibn Zuhayr, Qatadah, and Abu Hazrah, the same. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd also said this, and Ibn Zayd added: "The people of Yemen call the banana talh." Ibn Jarir mentioned only this view.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And extended shade.﴾ Al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Abdullah told us: Sufyan told us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆"

Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'raj, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Surayj told us: Fulayh told us, from Hilal ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider could travel for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆"

Al-Bukhari also narrated it likewise from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Fulayh with this wording. 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abu Hurayrah. And al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated it from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah. And 'Awf narrated it from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Hajjaj told us, both saying: Shu'bah told us: I heard Abu al-Dahhak narrate from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider would travel seventy or a hundred years. It is the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld)."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God, who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆"

Its chain is good, though they did not record it. Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise from Abu Kurayb, from 'Abdah and 'Abd al-Rahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, with the same wording. al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us: Mihran told us: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid told us, from Ziyad, the client of Banu Makhzum, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿And extended shade.⦆" When this reached Ka'b, he said: "He spoke the truth. By Him who sent down the Torah to Musa and the Furqan to Muhammad, if a man were to ride a four-year-old (haqqah) or a young camel (jadha'ah) and circle around the base of that tree, he would not reach its end until he collapsed from old age. God planted it with His own hand and breathed into it of His spirit. Its branches extend beyond the wall of Paradise, and there is no river in Paradise except that it flows out from the root of that tree."

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Muhammad ibn Minhal al-Darir told us: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ told us, from Sa'd ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it."

Al-Bukhari likewise narrated it from Rawh ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min, from Yazid ibn Zurayʿ. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it likewise from 'Imran ibn Dawar al-Qattan, from Qatadah with this wording. Ma'mar and Abu Hilal also narrated it from Qatadah with the same wording. Al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Sahl ibn Sa'd, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "In Paradise there is a tree that a swift, well-trained, galloping horseman could ride for a hundred years without crossing it."

This is an established hadith from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), indeed mutawatir, whose authenticity is firmly affirmed by the critical scholars of hadith, because of the multiplicity of its chains, the strength of its isnads, and the reliability of its narrators.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Bakr told us: Abu Husayn told us, saying: "We were at a gate in a certain place, and with us were Abu Salih and Shaqiq (meaning al-Dabbi). Abu Salih narrated, saying: Abu Hurayrah told me: 'In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for seventy years.'" Abu Salih said: "Do you call Abu Hurayrah a liar?" He replied: "I do not call Abu Hurayrah a liar, but I call you a liar." This displeased the reciters (qurra') on that day.

I say: Whoever denies this hadith has refuted himself, despite its being established, authentic, and traced back to the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj told us: Ziyad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Furat al-Qazzaz told us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "There is no tree in Paradise except that its trunk is of gold." Then he said: "Hasan gharib."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' told us: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi told us, from Zam'ah ibn Salih, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The extended shade is a tree in Paradise upon a trunk, whose shade is such that a rider would travel in its surroundings for a hundred years. The people of Paradise will go out to it, the people of the upper chambers (ghurraf) and others, and they will converse in its shade. Some of them will desire and mention the amusements of this world, and God will send a wind from Paradise, and that tree will move with every amusement of this world."

This is a strange report (athar gharib), and its chain is good, strong, and sound.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj told us: Ibn Yamani told us: Sufyan told us: Abu Ishaq told us, from 'Amr ibn Maymun concerning His words: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "Seventy thousand years." Ibn Jarir likewise narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan, the same. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "Five hundred thousand years."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us: Husayn ibn Nafi' told us, from al-Hasan concerning the words of God Most High: ﴿And extended shade⦆, who said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it."

'Awf said, from al-Hasan: "It has reached me that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it.'" Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn 'Abbas said, from 'Ikrimah, by way of Shabib: "In Paradise there is a tree that bears no fruit, under which one may shelter." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and Abu Hazra said, concerning His words ﴿and extended shade﴾, that it does not cease, and that there is in it neither sun nor heat, like the time before the break of dawn.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Paradise is sajsaj (a mild, temperate state), like the time between the break of dawn and sunrise."

The verses have already preceded, such as His words ﴿And We will admit them to shade, deep shade﴾ [An-Nisa 4:57], His words ﴿Its food is constant and its shade﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 13:35], His words ﴿In shades and springs﴾ [Al-Mursalat 77:41], and others besides these.

* *

As for His words ﴿and flowing water﴾, al-Thawri said: [meaning] it flows without a trench.

The discussion has already taken place at the explanation of His words ﴿therein are rivers of water unaltered﴾ [Muhammad 47:15], with what makes repeating it here unnecessary.

* *

As for His words ﴿and abundant fruit, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾, this means that they have abundant fruits, varied in colours, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿Whenever they are provided with a provision of fruit, they say: "This is what we were provided with before," and they are brought it in resemblance﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:25], meaning that the form resembles the form, but the taste is not the same taste.

In the two Sahihs, concerning the mention of the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), he said: "Its leaves are like the ears of elephants, and its fruits like the large jars of Hajar."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3207) and Sahih Muslim no. (162), from the hadith of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Also in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Malik, from Zayd, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The sun eclipsed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed, and the people prayed with him," and he mentioned the prayer. In it: they said, "O Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something in this place of yours, then we saw you draw back." He said: "I saw Paradise, and I took from it a cluster. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world endures."[[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1052) and Sahih Muslim no. (907).]]

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said: Abu Khaythama narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, Ibn 'Aqil narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: "While we were in the Zuhr prayer, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) advanced, so we advanced with him. Then he reached for something to take it, then he drew back. When he finished the prayer, Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you did something today in the prayer that you did not do before?' He said: 'Paradise was shown to me, with what it contains of splendour and radiance. I reached for a bunch of grapes to bring it to you, but it was kept from me. Had I brought it to you, you would have eaten from it for as long as heaven and earth endure, and it would not have diminished.'"[[The hadith was previously cited at the commentary on verse 35 of Surah al-Ra'd.]]

Muslim narrated, from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, something similar.[[The hadith has been cited in the previous place.]]

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn Bahr narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from 'Amir ibn Zayd al-Bakali, that he heard 'Utba ibn 'Abd al-Sulami say: "A Bedouin came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him about the Basin (al-Hawd), and he mentioned Paradise. Then the Bedouin said: 'Does it contain fruit?' He said: 'Yes, and in it is a tree called Tuba.'" He mentioned something I do not remember. He said: "What tree of our land does it resemble?" He said: "It does not resemble any tree of your land." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Have you come to al-Sham?" He said: "No." He said: "It resembles a tree in al-Sham called al-Jawza (the walnut), which grows on a single trunk, and its top spreads out." He said: "How large is its base?" He said: "If a young camel of your family's camels were to travel, it would not encircle its base until its neck was broken from old age." He said: "Does it have grapes?" He said: "Yes." He said: "How large is the cluster?" He said: "It is a month's journey for the speckled crow, and it never tires." He said: "How large is the grape?" He said: "Has your father ever slaughtered a billy goat of his flock that was very large?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he skinned its hide and gave it to your mother, and said: 'Make us a bucket from it?'" He said: "Yes." The Bedouin said: "Would that grape satisfy me and the people of my household?" He said: "Yes, and most of your clan."[[Al-Musnad (4/184).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿lā maqṭū'a wa lā mamnū'a﴾ (neither cut off nor forbidden), this means: they are not cut off in winter or in summer, but their fruit is constant and perpetual forever. Whenever they seek it, they find it. Nothing is withheld from them, by the power of Allah.

Qatada said: "No branch, no thorn and no distance prevents them from taking it." It has already been mentioned in the hadith: "When a man reaches for a fruit, another one returns in its place."

* *

As for His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, this means: high, soft and luxurious.

Al-Nasa'i and Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Rishdin ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "Their height is as between the heaven and the earth, and the distance between them is five hundred years."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2540). In it appears: "This is a hadith gharib (unusual, singly transmitted) which we do not know," and the word "hasan" is not in it, and likewise it appears in Tuhfat al-Ashraf.]]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib (sound but singly transmitted) hadith which we do not know except from the hadith of Rishdin ibn Sa'd." He said: "Some scholars said: the meaning of this hadith is the height of the couches in the ranks, and the distance between two ranks is as between the heaven and the earth."

Thus he (al-Tirmidhi) said that he does not know this except through the narration of Rishdin ibn Sa'd, who is the Egyptian, and he is weak. Likewise Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Rishdin.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/106).]] Then he (al-Tabari) and Ibn Abi Hatim both narrated it, both from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, and he mentioned it. Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Nu'aym ibn Hammad, from Ibn Wahb. Al-Diya' (al-Maqdisi) also transmitted it in Sifat al-Jannah, from the hadith of Harmala, from Ibn Wahb, with the like of it. Imam Ahmad narrated it from Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'a, who said: Darraj narrated to us, and he mentioned it.[[Al-Musnad (3/75).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from Abu Sahl (meaning Kathir ibn Ziyad), from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and raised couches﴾, he said: "The height of a man's couch among the people of Paradise is an eighty-year journey."

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, We created them with a [special] creation. And We made them virgins, loving, equal in age, for the companions of the right﴾, the pronoun refers to something not previously mentioned. But since the context indicates it, namely the mention of the couches, [it refers to] the women who recline upon them, that mention is sufficient and the pronoun returns to them. This is like His words: ﴿When there were displayed before him, in the evening, the swift steeds. He said: "Indeed, I have loved the love of good over the remembrance of my Lord," until they were hidden behind the veil﴾ [Sad 38:31-32], meaning the sun, according to the well-known view of the commentators.

Al-Akhfash said, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation﴾: he concealed them (the pronoun) and did not mention them before. Abu 'Ubayda said: they were mentioned in His words ﴿And [there are] wide-eyed maidens, like hidden pearls﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 56:22-23].

So His words ﴿Indeed, We created them﴾ mean: We restored them in the Hereafter's creation, after they had been old women with weak eyes and grey hair. They became virgins, loving (ʿuruban), that is, after being previously married they returned as virgins, loving (ʿuruban), that is, endearing to their husbands with sweetness, grace and beauty.[[In MS A: "ma kan 'ijaf rumsa" (they had been old, weak-eyed women).]]

Some said: ʿuruban means "playful and coquettish."

Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Rabadhi narrated from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation﴾: "They are old women who were in the world, weak-eyed and with sore eyelids." Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib (singly transmitted), and Musa and Yazid are weak."[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3296) and Tafsir al-Tabari (27/107).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Himsi narrated to us, Adam (meaning Ibn Abi Iyas) narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Jabir, from Yazid ibn Murra, from Salama ibn Yazid, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say regarding His words ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation﴾: meaning the previously married women and the virgins who were in the world."[[Narrated also by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/40) and Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah no. (389), through the chain of Shaybān. Jabir ibn Yazid is weak.]]

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, al-Mubarak ibn Fadala narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: "An old woman came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah that He admit me to Paradise.' He said: 'O mother of so-and-so, indeed Paradise is not entered by an old woman.' She turned away weeping. He said: 'Inform her that she will not enter it while she is old, for Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We created them with a creation. And We made them virgins﴾.'"

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it likewise in al-Shama'il from 'Abd ibn Humayd.[[Al-Shama'il al-Muhammadiyya of al-Tirmidhi no. (230).]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Bakr ibn Sahl al-Dimyati narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Hashim al-Bayruti narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abi Karima narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, from his mother, from Umm Salama, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me about Allah's words ﴿And [there are] wide-eyed maidens﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 56:22].' He said: 'Hur (wide-eyed): white. 'In (large-eyed): large of eyes; the eyelashes of the hawra' are like the wing of an eagle.' I said: 'Inform me about His words ﴿like hidden pearls﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah 56:23].' He said: 'Their clearness is the clearness of the pearl that is in the shells, which no hand has touched.' I said: 'Inform me about His words ﴿therein are good and beautiful [women]﴾ [Al-Rahman 55:70].' He said: 'Good in character, beautiful in face.' I said: 'Inform me about His words ﴿as if they were hidden eggs﴾ [Al-Saffat 37:49].' He said: 'Their delicacy is like the delicacy of the membrane which you see inside the eggshell next to the shell, which is al-ghirqi'.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, inform me about His words ﴿loving, equal in age﴾.' He said: 'They are those who were taken in the abode of this world as old women, grey-haired and with sore eyes. Allah created them after old age, and made them virgins, loving, passionate, endearing, equal in age, of one birth.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, are the women of this world better, or the wide-eyed maidens?' He said: 'Rather, the women of this world are better than the wide-eyed maidens, as the outer garment is better than the lining.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why is that?' He said: 'Because of their prayers, their fasting, and their worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah clothes their faces in light and their bodies in silk, white of colour, green of garments, yellow of ornaments. Their censers are of pearls, and their combs of gold. They say: "We are the eternal, so we never die. We are the joyful, so we are never miserable. We are the ones who remain, so we never depart. Indeed, we are the content, so we are never displeased. Blessed is the one for whom we are, and who is for us." ' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a woman among us marries two husbands, or three, or four, then dies and enters Paradise, and they enter with her. Who will be her husband?' He said: 'O Umm Salama, she will be given the choice, and she will choose the one with the best character. She will say: "O Lord, this one was the best in character with me, so marry me to him." O Umm Salama, good character has departed with the good of this world and the Hereafter.'"[[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/368). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/119): "In it is Isma'il ibn Abi Karima, whom Abu Hatim and Ibn 'Adi declared weak." In MS A: "O Umm Sulaym."]]

And in the long and well-known hadith of the Trumpet [[The hadith of the Trumpet has already been mentioned in the commentary on verse 73 of Surat al-An'am.]] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will intercede for all the believers to enter Paradise. Allah will say: "I have granted you intercession, and I have permitted them to enter it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "By He who sent me with the truth, you are not more knowing in the world of your wives and your dwellings than the people of Paradise are of their wives and their dwellings. A man among them will enter upon seventy-two wives: seventy whom Allah has created, and two from the offspring of Adam, who are superior to those whom Allah has created because of their worship of Allah in the world. He enters upon the first of them in a chamber of ruby, upon a throne of gold studded with pearls, on which are seventy mattresses of silk and brocade. He places his hand between her shoulders, then looks at his hand from her chest through her garments, her skin and her flesh, and he can see the marrow of her shin as you see the thread in a ruby tube. Her liver is a mirror for him, and his liver is a mirror for her. While he is with her, he does not tire of her and she does not tire of him, and each time he comes to her he finds her a virgin. His member does not slacken, and she does not complain of her private parts, except that there is no semen and no menstruation. While he is in this state, he is called: 'We have known that you do not tire and are not tired, but you have other wives besides her.' So he goes out and comes to them one by one, and each time he comes to one, she says: 'By Allah, there is nothing in Paradise better than you, and nothing in Paradise more beloved to me than you.'"

Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Hurairah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said to him: "Shall we have intercourse in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, with vigorous intercourse. When he rises from her, she returns pure and a virgin again." [[Narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 2633 (Mawarid), and Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 393, through Ibn Wahb. Darraj is criticised (mutakallam fihi).]]

Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim ibn Jabir al-Faqih al-Baghdadi narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Daqiq al-Wasiti narrated to us; Mu'alla ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti narrated to us; Sharik narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the people of Paradise have intercourse with their wives, they return as virgins." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (1/91). In it is Mu'alla ibn Abd al-Rahman, who is a liar (kadhdhab).]]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The believer in Paradise will be given the strength of such-and-such in regard to women." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will he be able to bear that?" He said: "He will be given the strength of a hundred."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud, and said: "Sahih, gharib." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 2012, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2536.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Husayn ibn Ali al-Ju'fi, from Za'idah, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurairah, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we reach our wives in Paradise?" He said: "A man reaches a hundred virgins in a single day." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir (2/12, 13).]]

The Hafiz Abu Abd Allah al-Maqdisi said: "This hadith, in my view, meets the conditions of the Sahih, and Allah knows best."

* *

His saying: ﴿ʿUruban﴾ (loving, devoted to their husbands). Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas: it means "those who make themselves beloved to their husbands." Do you not see the she-camel that is ḍubʿah (playful and coquettish)? She is like that.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas: "al-ʿUrub" are those who are passionate about their husbands, and their husbands are passionate about them. Likewise said Abd Allah ibn Sarjis, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Abu al-Aliyah, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, Atiyyah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

Thawr ibn Zayd narrated from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying ﴿ʿUruban﴾, and he said: "She is one who is coquettish with her husband (al-Milqah)."

Shu'bah narrated from Simak, from Ikrimah: "She is al-Ghanijah (one who is alluring and flirtatious)."

Al-Ajlah ibn Abd Allah narrated from Ikrimah: "She is al-Shakilah (one who is graceful in gesture)."

Salih ibn Hayyan narrated from Abd Allah ibn Buraydah concerning His saying ﴿ʿUruban﴾: "Al-Shikilah in the dialect of the people of Makkah, and al-Ghanijah in the dialect of the people of Madinah."

Tamim ibn Hadhlam said: "It is the goodness of conduct toward the husband (husn al-tabaʿʿul)."

Zayd ibn Aslam and his son Abd al-Rahman said: "Al-ʿUrub: the fine speech."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Sahl ibn Uthman al-Askari: Abu Ali narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, concerning ﴿ʿUruban﴾: "Their speech is Arabic." [[Note: the isnad here is as found in the text.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Atraban﴾ (of equal age). Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas: it means "of one age, thirty-three years."

Mujahid said: "Al-Atrab are those who are equal (al-mustawiyat)." In another report from him: "the similar ones." Atiyyah said: "the peers." Al-Suddi said: ﴿Atraban﴾ means: "in character, those who are bound in affection among themselves, with no hatred or envy among them, i.e., not like co-wives who were enemies in the world."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from Abd Allah ibn al-Kahf, from al-Hasan and Muhammad, concerning ﴿ʿUruban Atraban﴾, they said: "Those equal in age, who are in harmony together and play together."

Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a gathering place for the ḥūr ʿīn (wide-eyed, lovely maidens), who raise their voices with sounds never heard by creation. They say: 'We are the everlasting, so we shall never perish; we are the ones who live in bliss, so we shall never be miserable; we are the ones who are content, so we shall never be wrathful. Happy is he who is for us and we are for him.'" Then he said: "This is a hadith gharib."

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us; Isma'il ibn Umar narrated to us; Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from a certain Abd Allah ibn Rafi', from one of the sons of Anas ibn Malik, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The ḥūr ʿīn will sing in Paradise, saying: 'We are good and beautiful; we have been kept for noble husbands.'" [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Matalib al-ʿAliyah (4/402) and attributed it to Abu Ya'la; the editor quoted al-Busayri: "Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in it is a narrator who is unnamed." Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 254, by the same route.]]

I say: This Isma'il ibn Umar is Abu al-Mundhir al-Wasiti, one of the trustworthy and firm narrators. The Imam Abd al-Rahim ibn Ibrahim, known as Duhaym, also narrated this hadith, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Awn ibn al-Khattab ibn Abd Allah ibn Rafi', from a son of Anas, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The ḥūr ʿīn sing in Paradise: 'We are the fine companions, created for noble husbands.'" [[Narrated by Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 432, through Duhaym; by al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th, no. 420, through Ibn Abd al-Hakam; and by Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Ba'th, no. 75, through Kathir ibn Ubayd, all through Ibn Abi Fudayk. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, no. 4887, through al-Hasan ibn Dawud, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Awn ibn al-Khattab, from Anas, similarly. Al-Mundhiri said in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (4/226): "Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Tabarani narrated it, and its isnad is close (to sound). Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from a son of Anas who was not named, from Anas." Al-Bukhari pointed to a difference of opinion regarding it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (7/16).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿li-Ashab al-Yamin﴾ (for the companions of the right hand). That is: "We created them for the companions of the right hand," or "They were stored up for the companions of the right hand," or "They were wedded to the companions of the right hand." The most apparent view is that it is connected to His saying: ﴿Indeed We created them with a special creation. And We made them virgins, loving, of equal age, for the companions of the right hand﴾; so the meaning is: "We created them for the companions of the right hand." This is the interpretation of Ibn Jarir. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/109).]]

It is related from Abu Sulayman al-Darani, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: "I prayed one night, then sat making supplication. The cold was severe, so I began to supplicate with one hand, and sleep overcame me, and I slept. I saw a ḥūrāʾ (maiden) the like of whom had never been seen, and she was saying: 'O Abu Sulayman, do you supplicate with one hand while I am being nourished for you in bliss for five hundred years!'"

I say: It is possible that His saying ﴿li-Ashab al-Yamin﴾ is connected to what precedes it, namely His saying ﴿Atraban li-Ashab al-Yamin﴾, meaning: "of equal age among them," as came in the hadith which al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, from the hadith of Jarir, from Umarah ibn al-Qaqa', from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first company to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon; those who follow them will be on the brightness of the most brilliant star in the sky. They will not urinate or defecate, nor spit or blow their noses. Their combs are of gold, their perspiration is musk, their censers are of aloes wood, and their wives are the ḥūr ʿīn. Their character is that of one man, in the form of their father Adam, sixty cubits tall." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3327, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2834.]]

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun and Affan narrated to us, both saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, and al-Tabarani narrated it, and the wording is his, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise naked, beardless, with white skin, curly hair, and kohl-darkened eyes, being thirty or thirty-three years old, and they will be on the form of Adam, sixty cubits tall, with a breadth of seven cubits." [[Al-Musnad (2/295) and al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 4894.]]

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Imran al-Qattan, from Qatadah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise naked, beardless, kohl-eyed, being thirty or thirty-three years old." Then he said: "Hasan gharib." [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2545.]]

Ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever dies among the people of Paradise, young or old, will be returned at the age of thirty-three in Paradise, and they will never exceed that age. Likewise the people of the Fire."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Suwayd ibn Nasr, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Rishdin ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 2562, narrated from the route of Ibn Wahb; and Abu Nu'aym in Sifat al-Jannah, no. 259.]]
