Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 56, verse 75–82 (part 1 of 2):

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: "Indeed Allah does not swear by any of His creation; rather, it is an opening (istiftah) with which He begins His speech."

This view is weak. The view held by the majority is that it is an oath from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who swears by whatever He wills of His creation, and it is evidence of His greatness. Then some of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: "*La*" (لَا) here is superfluous (za'idah), and its implied meaning is: "I swear by the setting places of the stars." This was narrated by Ibn Jarir from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and its response (jawab) would be: ﴿Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾.

Others said: "*La*" is not superfluous and has no meaning of its own; rather, it is used at the beginning of an oath when the oath is sworn to a negated matter, like the statement of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her): "No, by Allah, the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the hand of a woman." Likewise here, the implied meaning of the speech is: "No, I swear by the setting places of the stars. The matter is not as you claim concerning the Qur'an, that it is magic or soothsaying; rather, it is a noble Qur'an."

Ibn Jarir said: Some of the people of the Arabic language (ahl al-'Arabiyyah, i.e., grammarians) said: the meaning of His words ﴿So I swear not﴾ is: "So the matter is not as you say." Then the oath was resumed afterward, so it was said: "I swear."

They differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿by the setting places of the stars﴾. Hakim ibn Jubayr narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that it means the stars of the Qur'an, for it was sent down all at once on the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) from the highest heaven to the lowest heaven, and then it was sent down piecemeal over the years after that. Then Ibn 'Abbas recited this verse.

al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: The Qur'an was sent down all at once from Allah, from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the noble scribe angels (al-safarah al-kiram al-katibin) in the lowest heaven. Then the scribe angels revealed it to Jibril in portions over twenty nights, and Jibril revealed it to Muhammad (ﷺ) over twenty years. This is His words: ﴿So I swear not by the setting places of the stars﴾, meaning the stars of the Qur'an.

'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Suddi and Abu Hamzah also said similarly.

Mujahid also said: ﴿by the setting places of the stars﴾ means in the sky, and it is said: their risings and their settings. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said similarly, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir. From Qatadah: its places (mawaqi'uha) means its stations (manaziluha). From al-Hasan also: the meaning is their scattering on the Day of Resurrection. al-Dahhak said: ﴿So I swear not by the setting places of the stars﴾ means by this: the *anwa'* (rising and setting seasons of the stars) which the people of the Jahiliyyah, when they were given rain, would say: "We have been given rain by the *nawʾ* of such and such."

* *

His words ﴿And indeed, it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾ mean: indeed this oath which I have sworn is a great oath; if you knew its greatness, you would magnify the one by whom it is sworn. ﴿Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an﴾ means: this Qur'an which was sent down upon Muhammad is a glorious book. ﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾ means: honored in a book that is honored, protected, and revered.

Ibn Jarir said: Isma'il ibn Musa told me, Shurayk informed us, from Hakim (who is Ibn Jubayr), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾, he said: "It is the Book that is in the heaven."

al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾ means: the angels. Anas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Abu al-Sha'tha' Jabir ibn Zayd, Abu Nahik, al-Suddi, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others also said similarly.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, Ma'mar told us, from Qatadah concerning ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾: "None touches it with Allah except the purified. As for in this world, it is touched by the impure Magian and the filthy hypocrite." He also said: "It is in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾" (with the *ma* negation, i.e., "It is not touched except by the purified").

Abu al-'Aliyah said: ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾ means: you are not the people of sins.

Ibn Zayd said: The disbelievers of Quraysh claimed that this Qur'an was brought down by the devils, so Allah informed that none touches it except the purified, as He said: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down. It is not befitting for them, nor are they able to. Indeed, they are removed from hearing it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 210–212].

This statement is a good statement, and it does not go outside the statements that came before it.

al-Farra' said: None finds its taste and benefit except the one who believes in it.

Others said: ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾ means: purified from major impurity (janabah) and minor impurity (hadath). They said: the wording of the verse is a report, but its meaning is a command. They said: the word "Qur'an" here refers to the *mushaf* (the physical copy), as Muslim narrated from Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade traveling with the Qur'an to the land of the enemy, lest the enemy obtain it. (Sahih Muslim, no. 1869, and it is also in Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2990.) They based this on what Imam Malik narrated in his *Muwatta'*, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm: that in the letter which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote to 'Amr ibn Hazm was: "None touches the Qur'an except one who is pure." (*Muwatta'* 1/199.) Abu Dawud also narrated in *al-Maraasil*, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, who said: "I read in a sheet with Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'And none touches the Qur'an except one who is pure.'" (*al-Maraasil*, no. 257.)

This is a good *wijadah* (a report found in a written record without direct hearing). Al-Zuhri and others have read it, and such a report should be acted upon. al-Daraqutni has traced it back (asnada) from 'Amr ibn Hazm, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, and 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, but there is scrutiny in the chain of each of them. (Sunan al-Daraqutni 1/122.) And Allah knows best.

* *

His words ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ mean: this Qur'an is sent down from [Allah], the Lord of the worlds. It is not as they say: that it is magic, or soothsaying, or poetry. Rather, it is the truth about which there is no doubt, and there is no truth beyond it that is beneficial.

* *

His words ﴿Then is it this discourse that you disdain?﴾ al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, "You deny it and do not believe it." al-Dahhak, Abu Hamzah and al-Suddi said similarly.

Mujahid said: ﴿mudhinun (disdaining)﴾ means: you want to flatter them concerning it and incline toward them.

﴿And you make your provision that you deny﴾. Some of them said: the meaning is: "you make your *rizq* (provision) in the sense of your *shukr* (thanks) that you deny," i.e., you deny instead of giving thanks.

It has been narrated from 'Ali and Ibn 'Abbas that they read it: "And you make your thanks that you deny," as will come.

Ibn Jarir said: It has been mentioned from al-Haytham ibn 'Adi that among the dialect of the Azd Shanu'ah: *ma ruziqa fulan* (what Fulan was provided) means *ma shakara fulan* (what Fulan thanked).

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Isra'il told us, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning ﴿And you make your provision﴾, that it means: "your thanks ﴿that you deny﴾, you say: 'We have been given rain by the *nawʾ* of such and such, by the star of such and such.'" (*al-Musnad* 1/108.)

This was narrated the same way by Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father, from Makhwal ibn Ibrahim al-Nahdi. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, and from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, all three from Isra'il, with the same chain, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ). (Tafsir al-Tabari 27/119.) Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it, from Ahmad ibn Mani', from Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi, with the same chain, and said: "Hasan gharib." Sufyan narrated it from 'Abd al-A'la without raising it. (Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3295.)

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, Shu'bah told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "No people were ever given rain except that some of them awoke as disbelievers, saying: 'We have been given rain by the *nawʾ* of such and such.'" And Ibn 'Abbas read: "And you make your thanks that you deny."

This is a sahih chain up to Ibn 'Abbas.

Others said: "*La*" is not superfluous and has no meaning of its own; rather, it is used at the beginning of an oath when the oath is sworn to a negated matter, like the statement of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her): "No, by Allah, the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the hand of a woman." Likewise here, the implied meaning of the speech is: "No, I swear by the setting places of the stars. Ibn Jarir said: Some of the people of the Arabic language (ahl al-'Arabiyyah, i.e., grammarians) said: the meaning of His words ﴿So I swear not﴾ is: "So the matter is not as you say." Then the oath was resumed afterward, so it was said: "I swear."

'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Suddi and Abu Hamzah also said similarly.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Sufyan informed us, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah (I think, or another), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard a man, while they were being given rain, say: "We have been given rain by some of the *'Ashanin al-Asad* (the stars of the Lion)." He said: "You have lied! Rather, it is the provision of Allah." (Tafsir al-Tabari 27/120.)

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Salih al-Sirari told me, Abu Jabir Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Azdi told us, Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr told us, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "No people are given rain on a night except that some people awake disbelieving because of it." Then he said: "﴿And you make your provision that you deny﴾: someone says, 'We have been given rain by the star of such and such.'" (Tafsir al-Tabari 27/120.)

In a hadith from Abu Sa'id, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) with the phrase: "If people were struck by drought for seven years and then it rained, they would say: 'We have been given rain by the star al-Mijdah'" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (3/7) and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih under no. (606) (Mawarid), by way of 'Amr ibn Dinar from 'Attab ibn Husayn from Abu Sa'id, with the wording: "If Allah were to withhold rain from the people for seven years and then send it down, a group among them would become disbelievers, saying: 'We have been given rain by the star al-Mijdah.'"]].

Mujahid said regarding ﴿And you make your provision that you deny﴾: it refers to their saying about the anwa' (the risings and settings of stars, a term for star-based weather beliefs): "We have been given rain by such-and-such a star, and by such-and-such a star." He said: Say instead: it is from Allah, and it is His provision. The same was said by al-Dahhak and others.

Qatadah said: As for al-Hasan, he used to say: "Evil is what a people have taken for themselves; they were given nothing from the Book of Allah except denial." So the meaning of al-Hasan's words is: you make your share of the Book of Allah that you deny it. For this reason, the verse before it says: ﴿Is it at this discourse that you are scornful? And you make your provision that you deny.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Why then, when it [the soul] reaches the throat﴾, i.e., the soul reaches the gullet (al-hulqum), meaning the throat, and that is at the time of death (al-ihtidar), as He said: ﴿No! When it reaches the collarbones. And it is said, "Who can cure him?" And he thinks it is the parting. And leg is wound about leg. To your Lord, that Day, is the driving.﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 26, 30]. Therefore He says here: ﴿while you, at that moment, are looking on﴾, i.e., at the dying person and what he suffers of the agonies of death.

﴿And We are nearer to him than you are﴾, i.e., through Our angels, ﴿but you do not see﴾, i.e., you do not see them. As He said in another verse: ﴿He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians, until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not fail [in their duty]. Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgement, and He is the swiftest of reckoners.﴾ [al-An'am: 61, 62].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then why not, if you are not to be held accountable, return it [the soul]﴾: its meaning is: Why then do you not return this soul, which has reached the throat, to its first place (in the text of M: "al-ula") and its abode in the body, if you are not to be held accountable?

Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning, "not to be called to account" (muhasabin). It is related from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Abu Hamzah, the same.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿if you are not to be held accountable﴾ means "not believing that you will be brought to account, raised up, and recompensed; so return this soul."

From Mujahid: ﴿not to be held accountable﴾ means "not certain" (ghayr muqinin).

Maymun ibn Mihran said: "not to be punished, subdued" (ghayr mu'adhdhabin maqhurin).

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿rawh﴾: it means ease and comfort, meaning a state of rest.

Mujahid likewise said: rawh means resting.

Abu Hazrah said: it means rest from this world. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: rawh means joy. From Mujahid: ﴿rawh and rayhan﴾: a Garden and ease. Qatadah said: rawh and mercy. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿rayhan﴾ means provision (rizq).

All these sayings are close in meaning and sound, for whoever dies among those brought near obtains all of that: mercy, comfort, rest, joy, happiness and goodly provision, ﴿and a Garden of delight﴾.

Abu al-Aliyah said: None of those brought near departs until a branch of the rayhan of Paradise is brought to him, and his soul is taken in it.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: No person dies until he knows whether he is among the people of Paradise or the people of the Fire.

We have already mentioned the hadiths about the dying person when commenting on His saying in Surat Ibrahim: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Ibrahim: 27]. It would be good to write them here as well. Among them is the hadith of Tamim al-Dari from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah says to the Angel of Death: 'Go to so-and-so and bring him to Me, for I have tested him with ease and hardship and found him to be what I love. Bring him to Me, for I will give him rest.' He said: The Angel of Death goes to him with five hundred angels, with them shrouds and perfume from Paradise, and with them bundles of rayhan, each stem of which has one root and twenty colours on its head, each colour having a scent different from the others, and with them white silk containing musk."

He mentioned the full hadith at length as has preceded. [See the commentary on Surat Ibrahim, verse 27.] Hadiths relating to this verse have also been transmitted. Imam Ahmad said:

Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Harun narrated to us, from Budayl ibn Maysarah, from Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, from Aisha, that she heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recite: ﴿fa-rawhun wa rayhan﴾ with the ra' vowelled with a damma (raf').

It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Harun, who is Ibn Musa al-A'war, with the same chain. al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know it except from his narration."

This reading is the reading of Ya'qub alone. The rest of the readers differed from him and read ﴿rawh﴾ with a fatha on the ra'.

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Abu al-Aswad Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Nawfal narrated to us: that he heard Durrah bint Mu'adh narrating from Umm Hani': that she asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Will we visit one another when we die and see one another?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The nafs (soul) will be a bird that hangs from the trees until the Day of Resurrection, when each soul enters its body."

This hadith contains good news for every believer. The word ya'lqu means "eats." It is also supported in authenticity by what Imam Ahmad narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, from Imam Malik ibn Anas, from al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The nasamah (soul) of the believer is only a bird that hangs in the trees of Paradise until Allah returns it to its body on the day He resurrects it." This is a great chain and a sound text.

It is in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take shelter in lamps suspended from the Throne." [The hadith has preceded in the commentary on verse 169 of Surat Al 'Imran, and see its takhrij there.]

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, who said: The first day I came to know Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, I saw an old man with white head and beard on a donkey, following a funeral. I heard him say: "So-and-so ibn so-and-so narrated to me, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever hates to meet Allah, Allah hates to meet him.'" He said: The people began to weep, and he said: "What makes you weep?" They said: "We dislike death." He said: "It is not that. Rather, when [the believer] is present at death: ﴿If he is among those brought near, then rest and ease and a Garden of delight﴾; when he is given this good news he loves to meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, loves to meet him. ﴿And if he is among the deniers, the astray, then a welcome of boiling water [and burning in Hell]﴾; when he is given this news he hates to meet Allah, and Allah hates to meet him."

Imam Ahmad narrated it thus [al-Musnad 4/259]. In the Sahih, a hadith from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) supports its meaning [Sahih Muslim, no. 2684].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if he is among the companions of the right﴾, meaning: and if the dying person is among the companions of the right, ﴿then, "Peace be upon you," from the companions of the right﴾, meaning: the angels give them this good news. They say to one of them: "Peace be upon you," meaning: there is no harm upon you, you are in safety, you are among the companions of the right.

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: he is safe from the punishment of Allah, and the angels of Allah greet him with peace. As Ikrimah said: the angels greet him with peace and inform him that he is among the companions of the right.

This is a good meaning, and it is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, saying: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and receive good news of Paradise which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. For you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you request, as a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [Fussilat: 30–32].

Al-Bukhari said: ﴿fa-salamun laka﴾ means: "Safe for you, that you are among the companions of the right." The word "inna" is omitted, and its meaning remains, as you say: "You are truly a traveller soon," when he has said: "I am travelling soon." It may also be like a supplication for him, as when you say: "Sawqan laka min al-rijal" [a watering for you from the men]. If you read "al-salam" with a damma, it is from the form of supplication [Sahih al-Bukhari 8/625, Fath].

Ibn Jarir has related this from some of the Arabic grammarians, and he inclined to it. And Allah knows best [Tafsir al-Tabari 27/123].

* *

His saying: ﴿And if he is among the deniers, the astray, then a welcome of boiling water and burning in Hell﴾, meaning: and if the dying person is among those who deny the truth, who are astray from guidance, ﴿then a welcome﴾, meaning a hospitality, ﴿of boiling water﴾, which is the molten liquid by which what is in their bellies and skins is melted, ﴿and burning in Hell﴾, meaning: a roasting of them in the Fire which surrounds them from all sides.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this is the certain truth﴾, meaning: indeed this report is the certain truth in which there is no doubt, and from which no one can escape.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾. Ahmad said:

Abu Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi narrated to us, my paternal uncle Iyas ibn Amir narrated to me, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾, he said: "Make it in your bowing (ruku')." And when [the verse] ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1] was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make it in your prostration (sujud)."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also narrated it likewise from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Musa ibn Ayyub, with the same chain [al-Musnad 4/155; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2869; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 887].

Rawh ibn Ubadah said: Hajjaj al-Sawwaf narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah, the Mighty, and praise be to Him,' a palm tree is planted for him in Paradise."

Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Rawh [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3464]. He and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3465; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10663, but al-Nasa'i narrated it from the route of Hammad ibn Salamah from Hajjaj al-Sawwaf, from Abu al-Zubayr, unlike al-Tirmidhi, who did not mention Hajjaj al-Sawwaf in this narration, so let this be noted]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr."

Al-Bukhari said at the end of his book: Ahmad ibn Ishkab narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa' narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; Glory be to Allah the Mighty."

The rest of the compilers, except Abu Dawud, narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, with his chain, the same [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7563; Sahih Muslim no. 2694; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3467; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10666; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3806].

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this is the certain truth﴾, meaning: indeed this report is the certain truth in which there is no doubt, and from which no one can escape.

﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾. Ahmad said:

Abu Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi narrated to us, my paternal uncle Iyas ibn Amir narrated to me, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) received: ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾, he said: "Make it in your bowing (ruku')." And when [the verse] ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la: 1] was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make it in your prostration (sujud)."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also narrated it likewise from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Musa ibn Ayyub, with the same chain [al-Musnad 4/155; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2869; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 887].

Rawh ibn Ubadah said: Hajjaj al-Sawwaf narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says: 'Glory be to Allah, the Mighty, and praise be to Him,' a palm tree is planted for him in Paradise."

Thus al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Rawh [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3464]. He and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3465; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10663, but al-Nasa'i narrated it from the route of Hammad ibn Salamah from Hajjaj al-Sawwaf, from Abu al-Zubayr, unlike al-Tirmidhi, who did not mention Hajjaj al-Sawwaf in this narration, so let this be noted]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr."

Al-Bukhari said at the end of his book: Ahmad ibn Ishkab narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, Umarah ibn al-Qa'qa' narrated to us, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him; Glory be to Allah the Mighty."

The rest of the compilers, except Abu Dawud, narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, with his chain, the same [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 7563; Sahih Muslim no. 2694; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3467; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10666; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3806].
